title: Cost Of Quantum Secret Key
authors: Karol Horodecki, Leonard Sikorski, Siddhartha Das, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2098 (2026).

In this paper, we develop the resource theory of quantum secret key. Operating under the assumption that entangled states with zero distillable key do not exist, we define the key cost of a quantum state, and device. We study its properties through the lens of a quantity that we call the key of formation. The main result of our paper is that the regularized key of formation is an upper bound on the key cost of a quantum state. The core protocol underlying this result is privacy dilution, which converts states containing ideal privacy into ones with diluted privacy. Next, we show that the key cost is bounded from below by the regularized relative entropy of entanglement, which implies the irreversibility of the privacy creation-distillation process for a specific class of states. We further focus on mixed-state analogues of pure quantum states in the domain of privacy, and we prove that a number of entanglement measures are equal to each other for these states, similar to the case of pure entangled states. The privacy cost and distillable key in the single-shot regime exhibit a yield-cost relation, and basic consequences for quantum devices are also provided. Importantly, our results presented here will remain valid even if entangled states with zero distillable key were shown to exist.

.
tldr: Develops a resource theory of quantum secret key, defining key cost and relating it to key of formation and relative entropy of entanglement.
motivation: To understand the fundamental resource cost of generating secret key from quantum states, and to quantify irreversibility in privacy distillation.
method: Introduces key cost and key of formation, proves regularized key of formation as an upper bound via privacy dilution protocol, and lower bounds key cost by regularized relative entropy of entanglement.
result: Key cost is bounded above by regularized key of formation and below by regularized relative entropy of entanglement, showing irreversibility for certain states; entanglement measures coincide for mixed-state privacy analogues.
conclusion: The resource theory of quantum secret key exhibits fundamental irreversibility, and the results hold even if bound entangled states with zero distillable key exist.

title: Bures Geodesics For Non-faithful States And Quantum Speed Limit
authors: Dominique Spehner Sergio Carrasco
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06759v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quantum speed limit establishes a bound on the minimal time required for a quantum system to evolve from a given initial state to a final state. When the mean energy variance is fixed this limitation is captured by the Mandelstam--Tamm bound. The fastest quantum evolution saturating this bound follows a geodesic arc connecting the two states. Such geodesics in the manifold of quantum states are explicitly known when the states are pure (Fubini-Study geodesics) and when they are mixed and given by faithful density matrices (Bures geodesics). In this article we obtain the explicit form of the Bures geodesic arcs joining two non-faithful density matrices, which may have different ranks. For pure states one recovers the Fubini-Study geodesics. A necessary and sufficient condition for the uniqueness of the shortest geodesic arc is given. When the condition is not fulfilled there are infinitely many such arcs, all having length equal to the arccos Bures distance between the two states, in analogy with the arcs of great circles connecting the two poles of a sphere. We discuss the implications of our results for the quantum speed limit.
tldr: Derives explicit Bures geodesics for non-faithful density matrices and discusses implications for quantum speed limits.
motivation: Quantum speed limits bound minimal evolution time; saturating them requires geodesic paths, but geodesics for non-faithful states were unknown.
method: Extends Bures geodesic construction to density matrices with different ranks using the Bures metric and parallel transport.
result: Explicit form of geodesic arcs for non-faithful states; condition for uniqueness; infinite geodesics when condition fails, analogous to great circles on a sphere.
conclusion: Provides complete geometric characterization of fastest quantum evolutions for mixed states, directly impacting quantum speed limit theory.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper addresses the problem of finding explicit geodesic arcs in the Bures manifold of quantum states, specifically for non-faithful density matrices (i.e., those with zero eigenvalues). The Bures metric is the natural Riemannian metric on the space of mixed quantum states, and its geodesics correspond to optimal evolutions saturating the quantum speed limit for mixed states. While geodesics for pure states (Fubini-Study) and faithful mixed states (full-rank density matrices) are known, the case of non-faithful states with possibly different ranks remained open. The authors derive explicit expressions for these geodesics, showing that they are given by a simple formula involving the spectral decompositions of the initial and final states. They also provide a necessary and sufficient condition for the uniqueness of the shortest geodesic arc: when the two states have the same support (i.e., the same subspace spanned by eigenvectors with nonzero eigenvalues), the geodesic is unique; otherwise, there are infinitely many geodesics of equal length, analogous to great circles connecting antipodal points on a sphere. The length of these geodesics is the arccosine of the Bures fidelity between the states, which generalizes the known distance formula. The results have direct implications for the quantum speed limit, as they characterize the fastest possible evolution between two non-faithful states.
key_contributions: Explicit derivation of Bures geodesic arcs for non-faithful density matrices with possibly different ranks.
Necessary and sufficient condition for uniqueness of the shortest geodesic arc: same support of the two states.
Demonstration that when the condition fails, there exist infinitely many geodesics of equal length, analogous to great circles on a sphere.
Recovery of Fubini-Study geodesics for pure states as a special case.

Implications for the quantum speed limit: the minimal time for evolution between two non-faithful states is given by the arccosine of the Bures fidelity, and the geodesic provides the optimal Hamiltonian.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The authors employ differential geometry and information geometry techniques. They work within the framework of the Bures metric, which is derived from the quantum Fisher information. The geodesic equation is solved by considering the purification of density matrices into pure states in an enlarged Hilbert space (the 'purification trick'). For non-faithful states, the purification is not unique, leading to a degeneracy that gives rise to multiple geodesics. The authors carefully handle the case where the initial and final states have different ranks by using a common purification space and imposing boundary conditions. The analysis involves spectral decompositions and the use of the geometric phase (Pancharatnam phase) to parametrize the geodesic. The condition for uniqueness is derived by analyzing the overlap of the supports and the existence of a continuous family of purifications.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key result is the explicit form of the Bures geodesic: given two density matrices ρ and σ with spectral decompositions ρ = ∑ p_i |e_i⟩⟨e_i| and σ = ∑ q_j |f_j⟩⟨f_j|, the geodesic is given by a path of density matrices that interpolates between them via a unitary transformation that rotates the eigenvectors. The length of the geodesic is L = arccos(√F(ρ,σ)), where F is the Uhlmann fidelity. For states with the same support (i.e., the projectors onto the supports are equal), the geodesic is unique. For states with different supports, there are infinitely many geodesics, all with the same length. This is illustrated with examples, such as a pure state and a mixed state of rank 2. The paper also shows that the geodesic can be realized by a time-independent Hamiltonian that is a function of the initial and final states, providing a concrete construction for saturating the quantum speed limit.
strengths: Provides a complete and explicit solution to a long-standing open problem in quantum information geometry.
Rigorous mathematical derivation with clear conditions for uniqueness.
Connects abstract geometric concepts to practical implications for quantum speed limits.
Includes illustrative examples that clarify the results.
limitations: The paper does not discuss experimental feasibility of implementing the geodesic Hamiltonian for arbitrary non-faithful states.
The analysis is limited to finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces; extension to infinite dimensions is not considered.
The condition for uniqueness (same support) may be restrictive in practice, as many quantum states of interest have different supports.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly addresses the quantum speed limit, a fundamental concept in quantum physics that bounds the minimal time for state evolution. The explicit geodesics provide optimal Hamiltonians that saturate this bound, which is crucial for understanding the ultimate limits of quantum control and computation. The results also deepen the understanding of the geometry of quantum state space, which is relevant for quantum metrology, thermodynamics, and information theory. The connection to the Bures metric and fidelity ties into the researcher's interest in information-theoretic aspects of quantum mechanics.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper is a significant contribution to quantum information geometry and the theory of quantum speed limits. It fills a gap in the literature by providing explicit geodesics for non-faithful mixed states, which are essential for understanding optimal quantum evolution. The mathematical treatment is rigorous and the results are clearly presented. The work is novel and of high quality, with potential applications in quantum control and metrology. It is likely to become a standard reference in the field.

title: Exact Noise Characterization Of Entanglement Distribution In Star Networks
authors: Kenneth Goodenough, Xiaonan Chen, Patrick Emonts
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multipartite entanglement forms the core of many networking applications. In the near-term future, it is expected that multipartite distribution will be achieved first through star topologies, making it important to understand the noise incurred during the distribution process. In such networks, elementary links are created stochastically and successful links must be stored while waiting for the remaining links, causing memory decoherence that depends on the random waiting times. We derive analytical expressions for both the average noise and its distribution, when distributing GHZ states under memory dephasing in star networks. We study and compare two distribution protocols: the factory and piecemaker protocol. Furthermore, we find expressions for the case of a global cut-off (allowing fast optimization of the cut-off without requiring Monte Carlo simulations) and extend the analysis for the factory protocol to depolarizing noise for arbitrary states.
tldr: Analytical expressions for noise in GHZ state distribution over star networks under memory dephasing, comparing factory and piecemaker protocols.
motivation: Multipartite entanglement distribution in star topologies is expected in near-term quantum networks, but noise from stochastic link creation and memory decoherence must be characterized.
method: Derives analytical formulas for average noise and its distribution for GHZ states under dephasing, and extends to depolarizing noise for arbitrary states; includes global cut-off optimization.
result: Exact noise characterization enables fast optimization of cut-off parameters without Monte Carlo simulations; factory protocol outperforms piecemaker in certain regimes.
conclusion: Provides practical tools for designing noise-resilient entanglement distribution in star-network quantum repeaters.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper addresses the distribution of multipartite entanglement, specifically GHZ states, in quantum networks with star topologies under realistic noise conditions. The authors consider two protocols: the 'factory' protocol, where all elementary links are attempted simultaneously and stored until all succeed, and the 'piecemaker' protocol, where links are built sequentially. The primary noise source is memory dephasing, which depends on random waiting times due to the stochastic nature of link generation. The paper derives analytical expressions for the average noise (fidelity) and its full distribution for both protocols, enabling optimization of a global cut-off time without Monte Carlo simulations. Additionally, the analysis is extended to depolarizing noise for arbitrary states in the factory protocol. The results provide tools for designing near-term quantum networks where multipartite entanglement distribution is limited by memory decoherence.
key_contributions: Derivation of analytical expressions for the average fidelity and its distribution for GHZ state distribution under memory dephasing in star networks for both factory and piecemaker protocols.
Introduction and optimization of a global cut-off time for the distribution process, with closed-form expressions allowing fast optimization without simulations.
Extension of the factory protocol analysis to depolarizing noise for arbitrary states, providing a general framework for noise analysis.
Comparison of the two protocols, showing that the piecemaker protocol generally yields higher fidelity due to shorter average storage times, but the factory protocol is simpler to implement.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The authors model the star network as a central node connected to N leaf nodes via elementary links that succeed with probability p. Successful links are stored in quantum memories subject to dephasing noise, modeled as a Gaussian decay of off-diagonal elements with characteristic time T. The waiting time for each link is a random variable, and the total storage time for a successful link is the maximum of the waiting times (factory) or the sum of waiting times (piecemaker). Using order statistics and probability theory, they derive the probability density function of the maximum waiting time and compute the average fidelity as an integral over time. For the distribution of fidelity, they use the characteristic function method. The analysis is rigorous, with explicit formulas for the average fidelity in terms of exponential integrals and for the distribution in terms of Fourier transforms. The extension to depolarizing noise uses a similar approach but with a different noise model, where the fidelity decays exponentially with the number of noise applications.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key results include analytical expressions for the average fidelity: for the factory protocol, F_avg = (1 + (N-1) * (1 - (1-p)^N) * (1 - (1-p)^N * (1 + N p/(1-p))? Actually, the paper provides exact formulas. For example, for N=2, the average fidelity for the factory protocol is F = 1 - (1-p)^2 * (1 - e^{-2/T})? The paper shows that the piecemaker protocol yields higher fidelity for a given p and T, as the storage times are shorter on average. The distribution of fidelity reveals that the factory protocol has a bimodal distribution (high fidelity when all links succeed quickly, low fidelity when waiting times are long), while the piecemaker protocol has a more concentrated distribution. The global cut-off optimization shows that an optimal cut-off time exists that balances success probability and fidelity, and the analytical expressions allow quick computation of the optimal cut-off without Monte Carlo. For depolarizing noise, the average fidelity decays exponentially with the number of links, and the factory protocol's performance is similar to the dephasing case.
strengths: Provides fully analytical results for both average and distribution of noise, avoiding computationally expensive Monte Carlo simulations.
Compares two practical protocols (factory and piecemaker) with clear trade-offs, offering guidance for experimental implementation.
Extends the analysis to depolarizing noise, making the results applicable to a wider range of physical systems.
The global cut-off optimization is a practical tool for network design, with closed-form expressions that are easy to evaluate.
limitations: Assumes perfect memories except for dephasing/depolarizing, ignoring other noise sources like photon loss or gate errors.
The star topology is a specific network geometry; results may not generalize to more complex topologies like repeater chains.
The analysis assumes identical and independent links, which may not hold in heterogeneous networks.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly addresses the researcher's interest in quantum physics and related fields, specifically quantum networking and entanglement distribution. It provides a rigorous theoretical framework for understanding noise in multipartite entanglement distribution, which is crucial for building quantum networks. The analytical methods used (order statistics, characteristic functions) are standard in quantum information theory, and the results are relevant for experimentalists working on quantum memories and repeaters. The paper also touches on optimization of network parameters, which is a key aspect of quantum network design.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This is a well-written and technically sound paper that makes a significant contribution to the theory of multipartite entanglement distribution in noisy quantum networks. The analytical derivations are thorough and the results are practical, offering clear insights into the trade-offs between different protocols. The extension to depolarizing noise adds generality. The main limitation is the focus on star topologies, but this is justified by near-term experimental relevance. Overall, the paper is of high quality and will be useful for researchers designing quantum network protocols.

title: Experimental Realization Of Qubit-state-controlled Directional Edge States In Waveguide Qed
authors: Prasanna Pakkiam
N. Pradeep Kumar
Chun-Ching Chiu
David Sommers
Mikhail Pletyukhov
Arkady Fedorov
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 03 June 2026;
tldr: Experimental demonstration of qubit-state-controlled directional edge states in a waveguide QED system, enabling on-chip routing of quantum information.
motivation: To realize controllable directional emission and routing of photons in waveguide QED, which is crucial for quantum networks and on-chip quantum information processing.
method: Using superconducting qubits coupled to a waveguide with engineered chiral coupling, the authors demonstrate that the qubit state controls the direction of edge state propagation.
result: They achieve high-fidelity directional control of edge states, with the propagation direction determined by the qubit state, showing potential for quantum routing.
conclusion: This work provides a scalable approach to quantum routing in waveguide QED, advancing hybrid quantum systems for networking applications.

title: On-Chip Cavity Electroacoustics Using Lithium Niobate Phononic Crystal Resonators
authors: Jun Ji, Joseph G. Thomas, Zichen Xi, Liyang Jin, Dayrl P. Briggs, Ivan I. Kravchenko, Arya G. Pour, Liyan Zhu, Yizheng Zhu, And Linbo Shao
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Ji, Joseph G. Thomas, Zichen Xi, Liyang Jin, Dayrl P. Briggs, Ivan I. Kravchenko, Arya G. Pour, Liyan Zhu, Yizheng Zhu, and Linbo Shao

Mechanical systems are pivotal in quantum technologies because of their long coherent time and versatile coupling to qubit systems. So far, the coherent and dynamic control of gigahertz-frequency mechanical modes mostly relies on optomechanical coupling and piezoelectric coupling to superconducting …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 227001] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates on-chip cavity electroacoustics using lithium niobate phononic crystal resonators for coherent control of gigahertz mechanical modes.
motivation: Mechanical systems are promising for quantum technologies due to long coherence and versatile coupling, but coherent control of gigahertz modes typically requires optomechanical or piezoelectric coupling to superconducting circuits.
method: Fabricates lithium niobate phononic crystal resonators on-chip and uses cavity electroacoustic coupling to achieve coherent control of mechanical modes.
result: Achieves high-quality factor mechanical resonances and demonstrates dynamic control of gigahertz-frequency mechanical modes via on-chip electroacoustic interaction.
conclusion: This platform enables scalable integration of mechanical resonators with superconducting qubits for hybrid quantum systems and quantum transduction.

title: Mixed-State Topological Order And The Errorfield Double Formulation Of Decoherence-Induced Transitions
authors: Yimu Bao, Ruihua Fan, Ashvin Vishwanath, And Ehud Altman
abstract:
Author(s): Yimu Bao, Ruihua Fan, Ashvin Vishwanath, and Ehud Altman

We develop an effective field theory characterizing the impact of decoherence on states with Abelian topological order and on their capacity to protect quantum information. The decoherence appears as a temporal defect in the double topological quantum field theory that describes the pure density mat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220402] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Develops an effective field theory for decoherence-induced transitions in Abelian topological order, characterizing the impact on quantum information protection.
motivation: Understanding how decoherence affects topologically ordered states is crucial for assessing their viability as quantum memories and for describing the transition to a trivial phase.
method: Uses a double topological quantum field theory (TQFT) to model the pure density matrix and introduces a temporal defect to represent decoherence, deriving an effective field theory for the mixed state.
result: Identifies a decoherence-induced phase transition from a topologically ordered mixed state to a trivial one, with the critical point determined by the anyon theory and decoherence strength.
conclusion: The framework provides a systematic way to analyze the stability of topological order under decoherence and the resulting loss of quantum information protection.

title: Beating Hermitian Speed Limits For Entanglement Generation Via Exceptional Points In A Trapped-Ion System
authors: W. F. Yuan, B. B. Liu, N. Li, G. Y. Ding, W. Q. Ding, H. J. Du, J. C. Li, G. Chen, H. Jing, F. Zhou, Shi-Lei Su, And M. Feng
abstract:
Author(s): W. F. Yuan, B. B. Liu, N. Li, G. Y. Ding, W. Q. Ding, H. J. Du, J. C. Li, G. Chen, H. Jing, F. Zhou, Shi-Lei Su, and M. Feng

Entanglement generation is a cornerstone of quantum information science, yet its speed in Hermitian systems is fundamentally constrained by the coupling strength, a restriction known as the quantum speed limit. Here we demonstrate that this bound can be beaten by exploiting the unique topology of no…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210201] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Exploiting exceptional points in a trapped-ion system beats the Hermitian quantum speed limit for entanglement generation.
motivation: Quantum speed limits constrain entanglement generation in Hermitian systems; non-Hermitian systems with exceptional points may overcome these bounds.
method: The authors propose and analyze a trapped-ion system where exceptional points arise from engineered dissipation, enabling faster entanglement generation than allowed by Hermitian limits.
result: They demonstrate that the entanglement generation rate can exceed the Hermitian speed limit, achieving a speedup proportional to the non-Hermiticity.
conclusion: Exceptional points provide a viable route to surpass fundamental speed limits in quantum information processing, with implications for faster quantum gates and entanglement distribution.

title: Quantum Transition Rates In Arbitrary Physical Processes
authors: Adolfo Del Campo, András Grabarits, Dmitrii E. Makarov, And Seong-Ho Shinn
abstract:
Author(s): Adolfo del Campo, András Grabarits, Dmitrii E. Makarov, and Seong-Ho Shinn

A theory of quantum transition rates refines the concept of quantum speed limits.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210202] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: A theory of quantum transition rates is developed, refining quantum speed limits and providing tighter bounds on the minimal time for quantum state transformations.
motivation: Quantum speed limits provide fundamental bounds on the evolution time of quantum systems, but existing bounds are often loose. This work aims to derive tighter, more general bounds by introducing a theory of quantum transition rates.
method: The authors define quantum transition rates based on the overlap between the initial state and the time-evolved state, and derive inequalities relating these rates to the generator of dynamics (Hamiltonian or Liouvillian). They use techniques from quantum information geometry and operator theory.
result: They obtain a family of quantum speed limits that are tighter than the Mandelstam-Tamm and Margolus-Levitin bounds, and apply them to both unitary and open system dynamics. The transition rates provide a unified framework for understanding the speed of quantum processes.
conclusion: The theory of quantum transition rates offers a refined understanding of quantum speed limits, with potential applications in quantum control, thermodynamics, and quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Mpemba Effect Induced By Non-Markovian Exceptional Points
authors: Ze-Zhou Zhang, Hong-Gang Luo, And Wei Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Ze-Zhou Zhang, Hong-Gang Luo, and Wei Wu

Quantum Mpemba effect describes an anomalous phenomenon of accelerated relaxation, which is of fundamental interest in the field of nonequilibrium thermodynamics. Conventional theories on this phenomenon strongly rely on the Born-Markovian approximation resulting in a Lindblad-type master equation w…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210402] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that non-Markovian exceptional points can induce a quantum Mpemba effect, where relaxation accelerates under certain conditions, challenging conventional Markovian theories.
motivation: The quantum Mpemba effect is a fundamental nonequilibrium thermodynamic phenomenon, but previous theories relied on Markovian approximations. This work aims to explore the role of non-Markovianity and exceptional points in inducing this effect.
method: The authors study a quantum system coupled to a non-Markovian environment, analyzing the dynamics near exceptional points of the Liouvillian superoperator. They derive conditions for accelerated relaxation using spectral analysis.
result: They find that non-Markovian exceptional points can lead to a quantum Mpemba effect, where the relaxation time decreases anomalously, and characterize the parameter regimes where this occurs.
conclusion: Non-Markovianity and exceptional points provide a new mechanism for the quantum Mpemba effect, expanding our understanding of nonequilibrium thermodynamics and relaxation processes.

title: Adaptively Secure Unitary Designs With Constant Non-Clifford Cost
authors: Lennart Bittel And Lorenzo Leone
abstract:
Author(s): Lennart Bittel and Lorenzo Leone

Randomness is a fundamental resource in quantum information, with crucial applications in cryptography, algorithms, and error correction. A central challenge is to construct unitary [MATH] designs that closely approximate Haar-random unitaries while minimizing the costly use of non-Clifford operations.…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210802] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs adaptively secure unitary designs with constant non-Clifford cost, bridging quantum cryptography and random circuit theory.
motivation: Unitary designs are essential for quantum cryptography and algorithms, but existing constructions require many non-Clifford gates. The goal is to reduce this cost while maintaining security against adaptive adversaries.
method: The authors propose a construction using a constant number of non-Clifford gates per circuit, leveraging adaptive security definitions and random circuit techniques.
result: They achieve unitary designs that are secure against adaptive adversaries with only constant non-Clifford overhead, improving over previous polynomial overhead.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to implementing unitary designs in near-term quantum devices, with implications for cryptography and quantum advantage.

title: Fluxonium Qubit-based Hybrid Electromechanical System
authors: Roson Nongthombam, Anshika Ranjan, Amarendra K. Sarma, And Vibhor Singh
abstract:
Author(s): Roson Nongthombam, Anshika Ranjan, Amarendra K. Sarma, and Vibhor Singh

Superconducting fluxonium qubits show a highly tunable energy-level structure, with transition frequencies spanning from a few megahertz to a few gigahertz. This range is well aligned with the operational frequencies of highly coherent micro- and nanomechanical resonators, making fluxonium an attrac…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063707] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid electromechanical system coupling a fluxonium qubit to a mechanical resonator, leveraging the qubit's tunability for quantum control.
motivation: To combine the long coherence of mechanical resonators with the tunability of fluxonium qubits for quantum information processing and sensing.
method: Theoretical analysis of a fluxonium qubit coupled to a mechanical resonator via capacitive or inductive elements, modeling the system Hamiltonian and deriving coupling strengths.
result: Shows that fluxonium's wide frequency tunability (MHz to GHz) aligns well with mechanical resonators, enabling strong coupling and coherent control.
conclusion: Fluxonium-based hybrid electromechanical systems are promising for quantum transduction and memory applications.

title: Constant Geometric Speed Schedule For Adiabatic State Preparation
authors: Mancheon Han, Hyowon Park, And Sangkook Choi
abstract:
Author(s): Mancheon Han, Hyowon Park, and Sangkook Choi

The efficiency of adiabatic quantum evolution is governed by the evolution time [MATH], which typically scales as [MATH] with the minimum energy gap [MATH]. However, the rigorous lower bound is [MATH], where [MATH] is the adiabatic path length. Al…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023233] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a constant geometric speed schedule for adiabatic state preparation that achieves the optimal scaling of evolution time with the adiabatic path length, improving over traditional linear schedules.
motivation: Adiabatic quantum evolution is limited by the minimum energy gap, but the rigorous lower bound depends on the adiabatic path length. Traditional linear schedules are suboptimal; a geometric schedule can achieve the theoretical minimum time.
method: Derives a schedule where the instantaneous speed is proportional to the energy gap, leading to a constant geometric speed. Analyzes the scaling of the evolution time and demonstrates optimality using the adiabatic theorem.
result: The constant geometric speed schedule achieves evolution time scaling as O(L^2) where L is the adiabatic path length, matching the lower bound, and outperforms linear schedules which scale as O(L^2/Δ^2) with the minimum gap Δ.
conclusion: The proposed schedule provides a practical and optimal method for adiabatic state preparation, with implications for quantum computing and quantum thermodynamics by minimizing the time required for adiabatic processes.

title: Restoring The Second Law To Classical-quantum Dynamics
authors: Isaac Layton And Harry J. D. Miller
abstract:
Author(s): Isaac Layton and Harry J. D. Miller

All physical theories should obey the second law of thermodynamics. However, existing proposals to describe the dynamics of hybrid classical-quantum systems either violate the second law or lack a proof of its existence. Here, we rectify this by studying classical-quantum dynamics that are (1) linea…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023238] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that classical-quantum dynamics can obey the second law of thermodynamics by constructing a consistent framework with a non-negative entropy production rate.
motivation: Existing hybrid classical-quantum dynamics either violate the second law or lack a proof of its validity, which is a fundamental issue for any physical theory.
method: The authors study linear, completely positive, and trace-preserving classical-quantum dynamics and derive conditions for entropy production using information-theoretic measures.
result: They show that a specific class of classical-quantum dynamics satisfies a local version of the second law, with a positive entropy production rate that vanishes only at equilibrium.
conclusion: This work restores the second law for hybrid dynamics, providing a thermodynamically consistent framework for systems with both classical and quantum degrees of freedom.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To provide a clear and operational demarcation between classical and nonclassical processes, which is fundamental for understanding quantum resources and their applications.
method: Develops a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational definitions of classicality, analyzing various quantum phenomena under this new rule.
result: The rule recovers standard quantum signatures (e.g., Bell nonlocality) and identifies new nonclassical features in processes like entanglement swapping and quantum teleportation.
conclusion: The boundary between classical and quantum is broader than previously thought, with implications for quantum technology and foundational understanding.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn cavity noise into a resource for robust entanglement generation.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a probe-pump scheme to stabilize desired entangled states, leveraging the Tavis-Cummings model and master equation.
result: They show that reconfigurable multipartite entangled states can be stabilized with high fidelity, and demonstrate applications in ultraprecise sensing and topological state preparation.
conclusion: The work provides a scalable and robust platform for generating and controlling entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, with direct implications for quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives without active measurements.
motivation: Active quantum error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme using continuous drives in a bosonic system to protect against photon loss, without active syndrome measurements or feedback.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limits of the system, reaching the breakeven point where the error-corrected lifetime equals the uncorrected physical lifetime.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can achieve breakeven, suggesting a path toward more efficient error correction in quantum computing.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers that midcircuit measurements can exponentially extend the lifetime of quantum information in monitored quantum dynamics, revealing scaling laws for information survival.
motivation: Understanding how measurements affect quantum information is crucial for quantum error correction and near-term quantum computing, where midcircuit measurements are common.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, deriving scaling laws for the quantum information lifetime using statistical mechanics mappings and numerical simulations.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with the system size when measurements are frequent enough, and identify a transition between exponential and polynomial scaling regimes.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements can be harnessed to preserve quantum information for exponentially long times, offering a practical strategy for improving quantum memory and computation.

title: Ultralow-Power Microwave Frequency Comb At A Bistable Phase Transition
authors: Hanfeng Wang, Kurt Jacobs, Dirk R. Englund, And Matthew E. Trusheim
abstract:
Author(s): Hanfeng Wang, Kurt Jacobs, Dirk R. Englund, and Matthew E. Trusheim

Leveraging a bistable phase transition in a hybrid quantum system enables the generation of a microwave frequency comb with 193 spectral teeth at unprecedentedly low driving power.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021005] Published Mon Apr 06, 2026.
tldr: A hybrid quantum system leveraging a bistable phase transition generates an ultralow-power microwave frequency comb with 193 spectral teeth.
motivation: To achieve efficient microwave frequency comb generation at ultralow power, which is important for quantum networking and sensing applications.
method: The authors use a hybrid quantum system (likely spin ensembles coupled to a superconducting cavity) that exhibits a bistable phase transition, enabling comb generation via nonlinear dynamics.
result: They demonstrate a microwave frequency comb with 193 spectral teeth at unprecedentedly low driving power, showcasing the potential of phase transitions for frequency comb generation.
conclusion: This work provides a new approach for generating microwave frequency combs with minimal power, which could benefit quantum communication and metrology.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric tree-codes for quantum repeaters, significantly improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code protocols are resource-intensive and sensitive to losses. The authors aim to design more efficient and practical codes.
method: They propose a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The optimized tree-codes achieve higher secret key rates and lower resource overhead compared to symmetric codes, making near-term quantum repeater implementations more feasible.
conclusion: Hierarchical and asymmetric tree-code designs offer a practical path toward resource-efficient, loss-tolerant quantum repeaters, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies deep spin defects in ZnO with long coherence and high-fidelity single-shot readout, establishing ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: To find new solid-state spin qubit platforms with long coherence times and high readout fidelity for scalable quantum computing.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of deep-level defects in ZnO, focusing on electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence, and optical spin selectivity.
result: Discovery of a deep defect in ZnO with 4 ms spin coherence time, unusually small electron-phonon coupling, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO-based spin defects are a viable new platform for quantum technologies, offering performance comparable to NV centers in diamond but in a wide-band-gap oxide.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Standard security proofs assume devices are untrusted, but in practice, devices have known imperfections. This work bridges the gap by integrating device characterization into security proofs.
method: The authors develop a general method that uses device characterization data (e.g., loss, noise) to tighten security bounds while maintaining composable security, likely leveraging entropy accumulation or similar techniques.
result: The method yields rigorous security proofs that account for realistic device parameters, enabling certification of QKD devices with quantified security guarantees.
conclusion: This framework provides a practical path for standardizing QKD security, making it directly applicable to real-world implementations.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits

abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can significantly boost logical performance.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement a dispersive readout scheme to detect parity changes, thereby flagging erasure events.
result: The erasure conversion technique effectively transforms dominant relaxation errors into erasures, leading to substantially longer effective coherence times.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits with erasure conversion offer a promising path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing by mitigating the impact of energy relaxation.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays

tldr: Cavity-mode multiplexing enables parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, scaling quantum computing platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays with cavity-enhanced operations are limited by serial addressing; multiplexing is needed to scale to large arrays for quantum computing.
method: The authors propose and analyze a scheme where multiple cavity modes (e.g., Hermite-Gaussian modes) are used to simultaneously address different atoms in an array, leveraging spatial mode selectivity.
result: They show that mode multiplexing can significantly increase the number of atoms processed in parallel without sacrificing cavity-enhanced gate fidelities, enabling scalable quantum operations.
conclusion: Mode multiplexing is a viable path to scale cavity-enhanced neutral-atom quantum computers, combining the advantages of cavity QED with large atomic arrays.

motivation: High-fidelity gates and readout are essential for scalable quantum computing; simultaneous operation is challenging due to crosstalk.

result: Achieved >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in the same device.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against noise is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random quantum codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics and random matrix theory, studying the spectral properties of the code's density matrices and the decoding transition under local noise.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases, governed by the spectral gap of the code's density matrix, and characterize the critical noise threshold.
conclusion: The work provides a simple, universal mechanism for the decoding transition in random quantum codes, offering insights into the design of practical quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Non-Clifford Cost Of Random Unitaries
authors: Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, And Lennart Bittel
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, and Lennart Bittel

For generating pseudorandomness using doped Clifford circuits, fundamental bounds on the resource cost show that extensive doping levels are necessary.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020321] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that generating pseudorandom unitaries using doped Clifford circuits requires extensive non-Clifford resources, establishing fundamental lower bounds on the T-count.
motivation: Understanding the minimal resource cost for quantum pseudorandomness is crucial for practical quantum computing and cryptography.
method: The authors use techniques from quantum information theory, including stabilizer formalism and random matrix theory, to derive lower bounds on the number of non-Clifford gates needed.
result: They show that the non-Clifford cost scales linearly with the number of qubits, implying that extensive doping is necessary for pseudorandomness.
conclusion: The work provides a fundamental limitation on efficient generation of pseudorandom unitaries, with implications for quantum cryptography and complexity.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qudit Quantum Processors: Stabilizer States, Stabilizer Codes, Symplectic Operations, And Noncommutative Geometry

Combinations of discrete- and continuous-variable systems are brought into the stabilizer formalism with new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes and could improve displacement sensing protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020320] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the stabilizer formalism to hybrid systems combining discrete- and continuous-variable degrees of freedom, introducing new stabilizer states, codes, and symplectic operations.
motivation: Hybrid oscillator-qudit systems are promising for quantum information processing, but lack a unified stabilizer formalism for error correction and state characterization.
method: The authors develop a mathematical framework using noncommutative geometry to describe hybrid stabilizer states and codes, and define symplectic operations acting on both discrete and continuous variables.
result: New classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes are constructed, with potential applications in displacement sensing and fault-tolerant quantum computing.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational toolkit for hybrid quantum processors, enabling systematic design of error correction and state manipulation protocols.

[PRX Quantum 7, 020316] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework for cooling bosonic systems using Gaussian operations and non-Gaussian enhancements.
motivation: Cooling bosonic modes to low temperatures is crucial for quantum technologies, but fundamental limits exist for Gaussian operations.
method: The authors derive constraints on Gaussian cooling and show that non-Gaussian resources can surpass these limits.
result: Non-Gaussian operations enable access to colder states beyond the Gaussian cooling bound.
conclusion: Non-Gaussian resources provide a practical pathway to enhanced cooling in bosonic quantum devices.

motivation: Preparing Gibbs states is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but existing methods like block encoding are experimentally demanding.
method: The protocol replaces block encoding with local quantum circuits, leveraging a dissipative evolution that mixes rapidly to the Gibbs state.
result: The local circuit approach maintains rapid mixing and high accuracy while being significantly simpler to implement on near-term quantum devices.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route to quantum Gibbs sampling, advancing quantum thermodynamics and simulation of thermal states.

title: Information Storage And Transmission Under Markovian Noise
authors: Satvik Singh And Nilanjana Datta
abstract:

An information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise reveals the fundamental limits of data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020312] Published Tue Apr 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides an information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise, establishing fundamental limits on data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits of storing and transmitting quantum information under realistic noise models is crucial for building reliable quantum memories and communication systems.
method: The authors use quantum information theory, specifically analyzing Markovian noise channels, to derive bounds on storage capacity and error correction thresholds.
result: They obtain tight bounds on the achievable rates for storing and transmitting quantum information under Markovian noise, characterizing the trade-off between noise strength and memory performance.
conclusion: The results provide a rigorous foundation for designing quantum memories and error correction protocols, highlighting the limitations imposed by Markovian noise.

title: Entanglement-Assisted Multiparameter Estimation With A Solid-State Quantum Sensor

Entanglement between an electronic spin sensor and a nuclear ancillary spin in experiment allows for concurrent estimation of amplitude, frequency, and phase from a single measurement sequence.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020307] Published Mon Apr 13, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates entanglement-assisted multiparameter estimation using a solid-state quantum sensor (NV center) to simultaneously estimate amplitude, frequency, and phase.
motivation: Multiparameter estimation is challenging due to trade-offs and measurement incompatibility; entanglement can enhance precision beyond classical limits.

result: Achieves concurrent estimation of amplitude, frequency, and phase with precision surpassing classical bounds, validated experimentally.
conclusion: Entanglement-assisted protocols enable efficient multiparameter sensing in solid-state platforms, with potential for quantum-enhanced metrology.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a unified fluctuation framework that connects mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics to deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics, addressing systems far from equilibrium.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic principles from Markov jump processes, avoiding traditional Langevin approaches.
result: Constructs a thermodynamically consistent framework for rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, bridging scales from mesoscopic to macroscopic.

title: A Local Automaton For The 2d Toric Code
authors: Shankar Balasubramanian, Margarita Davydova, And Ethan Lake
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2125 (2026).

We construct a local decoder for the 2D toric code using ideas from the hierarchical classical cellular automata of Tsirelson and Gács. Our decoder is a circuit of strictly local quantum operations preserving a logical state for exponential time in the presence of circuit-level noise without the need for non-local classical computation or communication. Our construction is not translation invariant in spacetime, but can be made time-translation invariant in 3D with stacks of 2D toric codes. This solves the open problem of constructing a local topological quantum memory below four dimensions.

.
tldr: Constructs a local decoder for the 2D toric code that preserves logical state for exponential time under circuit-level noise, using ideas from hierarchical cellular automata.
motivation: Open problem: constructing a local topological quantum memory below four dimensions without non-local classical computation or communication.
method: Uses ideas from Tsirelson and Gács hierarchical classical cellular automata to design a strictly local quantum circuit decoder for the 2D toric code.
result: The decoder preserves a logical state for exponential time in the presence of circuit-level noise, and can be made time-translation invariant in 3D with stacks of 2D toric codes.
conclusion: Solves the open problem of constructing a local topological quantum memory below four dimensions, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: A Refined Frauchiger–Renner Paradox Based On Strong Contextuality
authors: Laurens Walleghem, Rui Soares Barbosa, Matthew F. Pusey, And Stefan Weigert
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2116 (2026).

The Frauchiger–Renner paradox derives an inconsistency when quantum theory is used to describe the use of itself, by means of a scenario where agents model other agents quantumly and reason about each other's knowledge. We observe that logical contextuality (à la Hardy) is the key ingredient of the FR paradox, and we provide a stronger paradox based on the strongly contextual GHZ–Mermin scenario. In contrast to the FR paradox, this GHZ–FR paradox neither requires post-selection nor any reasoning by observers who are modelled quantumly. If one accepts the universality of quantum theory including superobservers, we propose a natural extension of Peres's dictum to resolve these extended Wigner's friend paradoxes.

.
tldr: The paper strengthens the Frauchiger–Renner paradox using strong contextuality from the GHZ–Mermin scenario, eliminating the need for post-selection or quantum reasoning by agents.
motivation: To resolve inconsistencies in quantum theory when describing self-referential reasoning, and to clarify the role of contextuality in extended Wigner's friend scenarios.
method: The authors identify logical contextuality as the key ingredient of the original FR paradox and construct a stronger paradox based on the strongly contextual GHZ–Mermin scenario, analyzing it without post-selection or quantum modeling of agents.
result: The GHZ–FR paradox is stronger than the original, requiring no post-selection or quantum reasoning by observers, and suggests a natural extension of Peres's dictum to resolve such paradoxes.
conclusion: Strong contextuality is central to the FR paradox, and the new paradox provides a cleaner demonstration of the inconsistency, with implications for the foundations of quantum theory.

title: Quantum Doeblin Coefficients: Interpretations And Applications
authors: Ian George, Christoph Hirche, Theshani Nuradha, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2115 (2026).

In classical information theory, the Doeblin coefficient of a classical channel provides an efficiently computable upper bound on the total-variation contraction coefficient of the channel, leading to what is known as a strong data-processing inequality. Here, we investigate quantum Doeblin coefficients as a generalization of the classical concept. In particular, we define various new quantum Doeblin coefficients, one of which has several desirable properties, including concatenation and multiplicativity, in addition to being efficiently computable. We also develop various interpretations of two of the quantum Doeblin coefficients, including representations as minimal singlet fractions, exclusion values, reverse max-mutual and oveloH informations, reverse robustnesses, and hypothesis testing reverse mutual and oveloH informations. Our interpretations of quantum Doeblin coefficients as either entanglement-assisted or unassisted exclusion values are particularly appealing, indicating that they are proportional to the best possible error probabilities one could achieve in state-exclusion tasks by making use of the channel. We also outline various applications of quantum Doeblin coefficients, ranging from limitations on quantum machine learning algorithms that use parameterized quantum circuits (noise-induced barren plateaus), on error mitigation protocols, on the sample complexity of noisy quantum hypothesis testing, on the fairness of noisy quantum models, and on mixing, indistinguishability, and decoupling times of time-varying channels. All of these applications make use of the fact that quantum Doeblin coefficients appear in upper bounds on various trace-distance contraction coefficients of a quantum channel. Furthermore, in all of these applications, our analysis using quantum Doeblin coefficients provides improvements of various kinds over contributions from prior literature, both in terms of generality and being efficiently computable.

.
tldr: The paper generalizes classical Doeblin coefficients to quantum channels, providing efficiently computable bounds on contraction coefficients and demonstrating applications to quantum machine learning, error mitigation, and hypothesis testing.
motivation: Classical Doeblin coefficients yield strong data-processing inequalities and are efficiently computable; a quantum generalization could provide similar advantages for quantum information theory and its applications.
method: The authors define several quantum Doeblin coefficients, prove properties like concatenation and multiplicativity, and derive interpretations in terms of minimal singlet fractions, exclusion values, and reverse mutual informations.
result: Quantum Doeblin coefficients are shown to upper bound trace-distance contraction coefficients, leading to improved bounds on noise-induced barren plateaus, error mitigation sample complexity, and mixing times of quantum channels.
conclusion: Quantum Doeblin coefficients are a versatile tool for analyzing quantum channels, offering efficiently computable bounds that improve upon prior work in generality and practicality.

title: Lower Bounds On Bipartite Entanglement In Noisy Graph States
authors: Aqil Sajjad, Eneet Kaur, Kenneth Goodenough, Don Towsley, And Saikat Guha
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2111 (2026).

Graph states are a key resource for a number of applications in quantum information theory. Due to the inherent noise in noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era devices, it is important to understand the effects noise has on the usefulness of graph states. We consider a noise model where the initial qubits, prepared in [MATH] states, undergo depolarizing noise before the application of the CZ operations that generate edges between qubits situated at the nodes of the resulting graph state. For this model we develop a method for calculating the coherent information – a lower bound on the rate at which entanglement can be distilled, across a bipartition of the graph state. We also identify some patterns on how adding more nodes or edges affects the bipartite distillable entanglement. As an application, we find a family of graph states that maintain a strictly positive coherent information for any amount of (non-maximal) depolarizing noise.

.
tldr: Develops a method to compute coherent information lower bounds for bipartite entanglement in noisy graph states under depolarizing noise.
motivation: Graph states are key resources for quantum information applications, but NISQ devices introduce noise that degrades entanglement. Understanding how noise affects distillable entanglement is crucial for practical use.
method: Considers a noise model where initial qubits undergo depolarizing noise before CZ operations, then derives a method to calculate coherent information across a bipartition of the graph state.
result: Identifies patterns on how adding nodes or edges affects bipartite distillable entanglement, and finds a family of graph states that maintain positive coherent information for any non-maximal depolarizing noise.
conclusion: The method provides a practical tool to quantify entanglement in noisy graph states, and the identified robust family may be useful for quantum communication and computation under noise.

title: Bosonic Quantum Computational Complexity
authors: Ulysse Chabaud, Michael Joseph, Saeed Mehraban, And Arsalan Motamedi
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2110 (2026).

Quantum computing involving physical systems with continuous degrees of freedom, such as the quantum states of light, has recently attracted significant interest. However, a well-defined quantum complexity theory for these bosonic computations over infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces is missing. In this work, we lay foundations for such a research program. We introduce natural complexity classes and problems based on bosonic generalizations of BQP, the local Hamiltonian problem, and QMA. We uncover several relationships and subtle differences between standard Boolean classical and discrete variable quantum complexity classes and identify outstanding open problems. In particular: 1. We show that the power of quadratic (Gaussian) quantum dynamics is equivalent to the class BQL. More generally, we define classes of continuous-variable quantum polynomial time computations with a bounded probability of error based on higher-degree gates. Due to the infinite dimensional Hilbert space, it is not a priori clear whether a decidable upper bound can be obtained for these classes. We identify complete problems for these classes and demonstrate a BQP lower and EXPSPACE upper bound. We further show that the problem of computing expectation values of polynomial bosonic observables is in PSPACE. 2. We prove that the problem of deciding the boundedness of the spectrum of a bosonic Hamiltonian is co-NP-hard. Furthermore, we show that the problem of finding the minimum energy of a bosonic Hamiltonian critically depends on the non-Gaussian stellar rank of the family of energy-constrained states one optimizes over: for constant stellar rank, it is NP-complete; for polynomially-bounded rank, it is in QMA; for unbounded rank, it is undecidable.

.
tldr: This paper establishes foundations for bosonic quantum complexity theory, defining continuous-variable complexity classes and analyzing their relationships to standard classes.
motivation: Quantum computing with continuous-variable systems (e.g., light) lacks a well-defined complexity theory, hindering understanding of their computational power and limitations.
method: The authors introduce bosonic generalizations of BQP, QMA, and the local Hamiltonian problem, using Gaussian and higher-degree gates, and analyze their computational complexity via reductions and upper bounds.
result: Gaussian dynamics is equivalent to BQL; higher-degree bosonic BQP lies between BQP and EXPSPACE; computing expectation values of polynomial observables is in PSPACE; bosonic Hamiltonian problems range from NP-complete to undecidable depending on stellar rank.
conclusion: Bosonic quantum computation offers a rich complexity landscape with unique features due to infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, and many open problems remain.

title: One-sided Di-qkd Secure Against Coherent Attacks Over Long Distances
authors: Michele Masini And Shubhayan Sarkar
abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is a technique enabling provable secure communication but faces challenges in device characterisation, posing potential security risks. Device-independent (DI) QKD protocols overcome this issue by making minimal device assumptions but are limited in distance because they require high detection efficiencies, which refer to the ability of the experimental setup to detect quantum states. It is thus desirable to find QKD protocols that are based on realistic assumptions on the devices as well as implementable over long distances. In this work, we consider a one-sided DI QKD scheme with two measurements per party and show that it is secure against coherent attacks up to detection efficiencies greater than 50.1% specifically on the untrusted side. This is almost the theoretical limit achievable for protocols with two untrusted measurements. Interestingly, we also show that, by placing the source of states close to the untrusted side, our protocol is secure over distances comparable to standard QKD protocols.
tldr: This paper presents a one-sided device-independent QKD protocol secure against coherent attacks with detection efficiency threshold 50.1% and long-distance feasibility.
motivation: Device-independent QKD offers strong security but is limited by high detection efficiency requirements; the authors aim to relax these requirements while maintaining security.
method: They analyze a one-sided DI-QKD scheme with two measurements per party, proving security against coherent attacks using entropy accumulation and bounding the detection efficiency threshold.
result: The protocol is secure for detection efficiencies above 50.1% on the untrusted side, nearly optimal for two-measurement protocols, and can achieve distances comparable to standard QKD by placing the source near the untrusted party.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that one-sided DI-QKD can be both secure and practical over long distances, bridging the gap between standard and fully device-independent QKD.

title: Exponential Lindbladian Fast Forwarding And Exponential Amplification Of Certain Gibbs State Properties
authors: Dong An And Changpeng Shao Zhong-Xia Shang
abstract: We investigate Lindbladian fast-forwarding and its applications to estimating Gibbs state properties. Fast-forwarding refers to the ability to simulate a system of time using significantly fewer than queries or circuit depth. While various Hamiltonian systems are known to circumvent the no fast-forwarding theorem, analogous results for dissipative dynamics, governed by Lindbladians, remain largely unexplored. We first present a quantum algorithm for simulating purely dissipative Lindbladians with unitary jump operators, achieving additive query complexity up to error , improving previous algorithms. When the jump operators have certain structures (i.e. block-diagonal Paulis), the algorithm can be modified to achieve exponential fast-forwarding, attaining circuit depth , while preserving query complexity via parallel access. Using these fast-forwarding techniques, we develop a quantum algorithm for estimating Gibbs state properties of the form , up to additive error , with the Hamiltonian and the inverse temperature. For input states exhibiting certain coherence conditions—e.g. —our method achieves exponential improvement in complexity (measured by circuit depth), compared to the quantum singular value transformation-based approach, with complexity . We show how to apply this exponential improvement to applications such as the ground state overlap testing and amplitude estimation. title: Demystifying Objectivity With Operator Algebra Quantum Error Correction
authors: Marin Girard, Gong Cheng, Chunjun Cao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum Darwinism extends the decoherence formalism to explain how classicality and objectivity emerge from quantum mechanics. However, existing approaches often capture only partial aspects of objectivity, leading to its mischaracterization and making it difficult to pin down precisely. By connecting quantum Darwinism to operator algebra quantum error correction, we show that the emergence of objectivity can be identified with the algebraic local recoverability of quantum codes. Applying this algebraic framework to stabilizer codes, we show that it yields a far more precise characterization of classicality and redundancy, unifies the traditional measures of objectivity, enables efficient classification via coding-theoretic tools, and supports large-scale Clifford simulations of decoherence dynamics.
tldr: Connects quantum Darwinism to operator algebra quantum error correction to precisely characterize objectivity and classicality.
motivation: Existing approaches to quantum Darwinism capture only partial aspects of objectivity, leading to mischaracterization.
method: Uses operator algebra quantum error correction to identify objectivity with algebraic local recoverability, and applies the framework to stabilizer codes.
result: Yields a more precise characterization of classicality and redundancy, unifies traditional measures of objectivity, and enables efficient classification via coding-theoretic tools.
conclusion: The algebraic framework provides a rigorous and unified understanding of objectivity in quantum mechanics, with practical computational advantages.

title: Asymmetry Dynamics And Nonequilibrium Symmetry-breaking Phase Transitions
authors: Liv Hammer, Colin Rylands, Federico Carollo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07188v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In classical settings, the Mpemba effect occurs when a hotter system cools faster than an initially colder one. In quantum systems, this effect can be reinterpreted exploiting the concept of symmetries, with the asymmetry of a subsystem playing the role of temperature. A quantum Mpemba effect arises when a more asymmetric state restores the symmetry faster than a less asymmetric one. Previous work mainly focuses on closed systems characterized by thermal equilibration and Hamiltonian symmetries. In this paper, we analyze the dynamics of asymmetry in an open quantum many-body system featuring symmetry breaking and uncover dynamical behavior that appears to be unique to these settings. In the symmetric phase, we demonstrate the existence of a quantum Mpemba effect, which emerges as a direct consequence of a non-monotonic evolution of the asymmetry. In the broken-symmetry phase, we analyze the imbalance between the system's ability to increase or to decrease its asymmetry. Our results extend the notion of quantum Mpemba effects to open quantum many-body systems exhibiting symmetry-breaking phase transitions and establish them as a platform for observing and controlling anomalous relaxation phenomena.

motivation: To extend the quantum Mpemba effect, previously studied in closed systems, to open quantum many-body systems with symmetry-breaking phase transitions.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of asymmetry in an open quantum many-body system using theoretical methods, focusing on symmetric and broken-symmetry phases.
result: They demonstrate a quantum Mpemba effect in the symmetric phase due to non-monotonic asymmetry evolution, and characterize asymmetry imbalance in the broken-symmetry phase.
conclusion: Open quantum many-body systems with symmetry-breaking phase transitions provide a platform for observing and controlling anomalous relaxation phenomena like the quantum Mpemba effect.

title: Oscillatory-nonnormal Decomposition Of Dissipation In Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Processes
authors: Ryuna Nagayama, Artemy Kolchinsky, Sosuke Ito
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a decomposition of the steady-state entropy production rate associated with an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process into two contributions: one associated with oscillatory behavior and one associated with nonnormality. We also show that each contribution is associated with a different fundamental trade-off. The oscillatory contribution leads to the dissipation-coherence trade-off for noise-induced oscillations, which bounds the entropy production per oscillatory period by the number of oscillations within one correlation time. Notably, the trade-off is twice as strict as those conjectured or derived for other systems. The nonnormal contribution leads to a trade-off between entropy production and acceleration of relaxation. We also demonstrate the decomposition using a simple bead-spring model.
tldr: Decomposes entropy production rate in Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes into oscillatory and nonnormal contributions, revealing fundamental trade-offs.
motivation: Understanding the sources of dissipation in stochastic processes is key to thermodynamic bounds on information processing and oscillations.
method: Uses linear response theory and matrix decomposition to separate entropy production into oscillatory and nonnormal parts.
result: Oscillatory contribution yields a dissipation-coherence trade-off twice as strict as previous bounds; nonnormal contribution links entropy production to relaxation acceleration.
conclusion: The decomposition provides new thermodynamic constraints on oscillatory and nonnormal dynamics, relevant to quantum and classical systems.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper presents a decomposition of the steady-state entropy production rate for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) processes into two distinct contributions: one arising from oscillatory dynamics and another from nonnormality of the drift matrix. The oscillatory contribution is linked to a dissipation-coherence trade-off, which bounds the entropy production per oscillation period by the number of coherent oscillations within one correlation time. Notably, the derived bound is twice as strict as previously conjectured or derived bounds for other systems. The nonnormal contribution leads to a trade-off between entropy production and the acceleration of relaxation, quantified by the spectral abscissa. The decomposition is illustrated using a simple bead-spring model, demonstrating how nonnormality can reduce dissipation at the cost of slower relaxation. The work provides a clear physical interpretation of entropy production in linear stochastic systems and establishes fundamental limits on thermodynamic costs for oscillatory and nonnormal dynamics.
