title: Sensing Ac Fields With Quantum Many-body Scars
authors: Matheus Fibger, Andrei Tsypilnikov, Thiago R. de Oliveira, Fernando Iemini
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum many-body scars (MBS) exhibit weak ergodicity breaking and long-lived coherent dynamics within an otherwise thermal spectrum. We investigate their metrological properties using the quantum Fisher information (QFI), focusing on estimating the amplitude of a weak AC field in the PXP model. We show that the approximately uniform energy spacing of the scar tower enables collective resonant processes when the driving frequency matches integer multiples of the scar gap, resulting in a quadratic-in-time growth of the QFI over an extended time window. We analyze how the connectivity induced by different probe operators shapes sensing performance and demonstrate that staggered magnetization leads to a more favorable growth of the QFI with system size than homogeneous magnetization. Through frequency scanning and finite-size analysis, we characterize the scaling of the QFI with the number of particles. Finally, we develop a single-tower approximation under resonant driving, deriving a compact analytical expression that captures the time dependence and system-size scaling of the QFI. Our results establish how to leverage structured non-ergodic dynamics in quantum sensing protocols.
tldr: This paper explores the use of quantum many-body scars in the PXP model for sensing weak AC fields, leveraging their non-ergodic dynamics to achieve quadratic-in-time growth of quantum Fisher information.
motivation: Quantum many-body scars offer long-lived coherent dynamics in an otherwise thermal spectrum, which could be harnessed for quantum sensing beyond standard limits.
method: The authors compute the quantum Fisher information for estimating AC field amplitude in the PXP model, analyze the effect of probe operators (staggered vs. homogeneous magnetization), and develop a single-tower approximation under resonant driving.
result: They find that resonant driving at multiples of the scar gap leads to quadratic-in-time QFI growth, and staggered magnetization yields better scaling with system size than homogeneous magnetization.
conclusion: Structured non-ergodic dynamics in quantum many-body scars can be exploited for enhanced quantum sensing, with analytical expressions capturing the scaling behavior.

title: Contacting Josephson Junctions Via Airbridges In Superconducting Circuits
authors: Prakiran Baidya, Mom\v{c}ilo Milosavljevi\'c, Murali Krishna Kurmapu, Thomas F\"osel, Harshanth Ram Murugesan, Victor Kemme, Mojahed Jaber, Markus Sondermann, Christopher Eichler
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superconducting circuit devices require electrical interconnects between different circuit elements on the chip, for which conventional device architectures use a combination of two structural elements: to connect non-adjacent elements in the base layer, and to connect the electrodes forming the Josephson junctions to the base layer. Bandages introduce unwanted parasitic material interfaces and increase the manufacturing complexity. Here, we overcome the limitations imposed by by establishing electrical interconnects with airbridges of varying size fabricated in a single step. The airbridges show a high yield and mechanical stability over a wide range of sizes from [MATH] to [MATH] in width and from [MATH] to [MATH] in length, and show low loss when integrated in coplanar waveguide resonators and transmon qubits. Measured relaxation times up to more than [MATH] in standard transmon geometries show that the process achieves high coherence while substantially easing and accelerating device fabrication.
tldr: This paper presents a single-step fabrication of airbridges for interconnects in superconducting circuits, achieving high coherence and simplifying fabrication.
motivation: Conventional interconnects in superconducting circuits introduce parasitic interfaces and increase complexity; a simpler, low-loss interconnect method is needed.
method: Airbridges of varying sizes are fabricated in a single step and integrated into coplanar waveguide resonators and transmon qubits; their mechanical stability and microwave performance are characterized.
result: Airbridges show high yield, mechanical stability, and low loss; transmon qubits with these airbridges achieve relaxation times over 100 μs.
conclusion: The airbridge technique simplifies fabrication while maintaining high coherence, making it a promising interconnect solution for superconducting quantum circuits.

When integrated into coplanar waveguide resonators and transmon qubits, the airbridges exhibit low loss, with measured relaxation times exceeding 250 μs in standard transmon geometries. This method simplifies device fabrication while maintaining high coherence, offering a practical improvement for superconducting quantum circuits.

title: Nonreciprocal Optomechanical Entanglement In An Asymmetric Fabry-Perot Cavity
authors: Jia-Kang Wu, Ning Hu, Jie-Qiao Liao, Xun-Wei Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonreciprocal transmission (classical nonreciprocity) in optomechanical systems based on asymmetric Fabry-Perot (F-P) cavities has been theoretically proposed and experimentally demonstrated. However, nonreciprocal quantum effects, particularly nonreciprocal quantum entanglement, remain unexplored in such systems. Here, we propose to generate nonreciprocal optomechanical entanglement in an asymmetric F-P cavity and discuss the connection between the nonreciprocal transmission and nonreciprocal quantum entanglement. We reproduce the nonreciprocal transmission spectra by solving the quantum Langevin equations, and then discuss the optimal parameters to achieve nonreciprocal optomechanical entanglement in the system. We show that a greater and more robust optomechanical entanglement can be approached in the asymmetric F-P cavities, in comparing with the symmetric cavities. Furthermore, we find that the degrees of classical and quantum nonreciprocities do not exhibit positive correlation as expected. Our work shows that the classical and quantum nonreciprocities can be realized simultaneously in the asymmetric F-P cavities, which provide a platform to explore the connection between classical and quantum nonreciprocities.
tldr: The paper proposes generating nonreciprocal optomechanical entanglement in an asymmetric Fabry-Perot cavity, exploring the connection between classical and quantum nonreciprocity.
motivation: Nonreciprocal quantum entanglement has not been explored in asymmetric Fabry-Perot cavities, and understanding the relationship between classical and quantum nonreciprocity is of fundamental interest.
method: The authors solve quantum Langevin equations to model the optomechanical system and compute entanglement measures, comparing symmetric and asymmetric cavity configurations.
result: Asymmetric cavities yield greater and more robust optomechanical entanglement, and classical and quantum nonreciprocities do not show a positive correlation.
conclusion: Asymmetric Fabry-Perot cavities provide a platform to simultaneously realize classical and quantum nonreciprocities, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

While classical nonreciprocity (nonreciprocal transmission) has been studied in such systems, quantum nonreciprocal effects, especially entanglement, remain unexplored. The authors model the system using quantum Langevin equations and derive the covariance matrix to quantify optomechanical entanglement via logarithmic negativity. They reproduce classical nonreciprocal transmission spectra and identify optimal parameters (e.g., cavity decay rates, mechanical damping, driving strengths) for achieving nonreciprocal entanglement. A key finding is that asymmetric cavities yield stronger and more robust entanglement compared to symmetric ones. Surprisingly, the degree of classical nonreciprocity (transmission contrast) does not positively correlate with quantum nonreciprocity (entanglement asymmetry), indicating a nontrivial relationship between classical and quantum nonreciprocities. The work provides a platform to explore this connection and demonstrates simultaneous realization of both effects.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of Free-Space Unidimensional Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution Under High Detector Noise
authors: Rachita Nandan, Jayanth Ramakrishnan, Shashi Prabhakar, R. P. Singh
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07206v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD), which uses quadratures of the electromagnetic field, enables practical quantum communication using standard telecommunication technologies. Unidimensional CV-QKD (UD-CVQKD) simplifies the implementation by restricting modulation to a single quadrature. In this work, we experimentally demonstrate a free-space Gaussian-modulated UD-CVQKD system operating under a high detector electronic-noise regime (1.4 shot-noise units). The system employs polarized coherent states with signal and local oscillator co-propagating in the same spatial mode in orthogonal polarizations, ensuring stable interference. System security is analyzed under both untrusted (UTD) and trusted (TD) detector noise models. While no positive secret key rate is obtained under the UTD model, the TD model enables secure key generation over a finite range of modulation variances, highlighting the critical role of detector trust in high-noise conditions. A maximum secret key rate of 270 kbps is achieved at an optimal modulation variance of 11.57. Furthermore, secure operation requires high-transmittance (low-loss) channels under such noise conditions. This study demonstrates the practical feasibility of free-space UD-CVQKD in realistic high electronic-noise detection constraints and highlights detector electronic noise as a key limiting factor in practical systems.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of free-space unidimensional continuous-variable QKD under high detector noise, achieving secure key rates with trusted detector noise model.
motivation: CV-QKD offers practical quantum communication using standard telecom tech, but unidimensional CV-QKD simplifies implementation. High detector noise is a key limiting factor in practical systems, and this work tests feasibility under such conditions.
method: Free-space Gaussian-modulated UD-CVQKD system with polarized coherent states and co-propagating signal and local oscillator in orthogonal polarizations. Security analyzed under untrusted and trusted detector noise models.
result: No positive key rate under untrusted detector noise model, but trusted model yields up to 270 kbps at optimal modulation variance 11.57, requiring high-transmittance channels.
conclusion: Free-space UD-CVQKD is practically feasible under high electronic noise if detector is trusted, highlighting detector noise as a critical limitation.

deep_read.methodology_analysis: The experimental setup uses a continuous-wave laser at 1550 nm, with the signal and local oscillator (LO) generated from the same source. The signal is Gaussian-modulated in one quadrature using an amplitude modulator, and the LO is delayed and combined with the signal in orthogonal polarizations. The receiver employs a polarization-diverse heterodyne detection system with two balanced detectors. The electronic noise is measured to be 1.4 shot-noise units, which is high. Security analysis follows the asymptotic composable security framework, considering both untrusted (where detector noise is attributed to Eve) and trusted (where detector noise is known and trusted) models. The secret key rate is computed as a function of modulation variance and channel transmittance, using the reverse reconciliation protocol. The analysis assumes collective attacks and uses the Gaussian optimality theorem.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key result is that under the untrusted detector noise model, the secret key rate is zero for all modulation variances, indicating that high electronic noise cannot be tolerated if Eve controls the detector. Under the trusted detector noise model, positive key rates are obtained for modulation variances between approximately 2 and 20, with a maximum of 270 kbps at modulation variance 11.57. The optimal modulation variance balances the increase in mutual information with the increase in noise leakage. The paper also shows that for a given electronic noise, the channel transmittance must be above a threshold (e.g., >0.8 for 1.4 SNU) to achieve positive key rates. The results are presented in figures showing key rate vs. modulation variance and vs. channel transmittance. The experimental parameters are clearly stated, and the data points are consistent with theoretical predictions.
strengths: Clear experimental demonstration of a practical free-space CV-QKD system under realistic high-noise conditions.
Rigorous security analysis comparing trusted and untrusted detector noise models, highlighting the importance of detector characterization.
Achievement of a high secret key rate (270 kbps) despite high electronic noise, demonstrating practical viability.
Well-structured presentation with clear figures and parameter values.
limitations: The security analysis is asymptotic and does not account for finite-size effects, which could reduce the key rate in practice.
The system operates only under high-transmittance channels (low loss), limiting its applicability to long-distance or high-loss scenarios.
The trusted detector noise model assumes perfect knowledge of the noise, which may be challenging to achieve in practice.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly addresses the researcher's interest in quantum physics and quantum communication, specifically in continuous-variable quantum key distribution. It explores the practical challenges of implementing CV-QKD in free-space with high electronic noise, which is a key issue for real-world deployment. The comparison of trusted vs. untrusted detector noise models provides insights into security assumptions, relevant to quantum information theory. The experimental demonstration of UD-CVQKD advances the state of the art in practical quantum cryptography.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper presents a significant experimental achievement in free-space CV-QKD, demonstrating that secure key generation is possible under high detector electronic noise when the noise is trusted. The results are novel and provide valuable insights for practical system design. The methodology is sound, and the analysis is thorough. The main limitation is the asymptotic security analysis and the requirement for low-loss channels. Overall, this work is a meaningful contribution to the field of quantum cryptography and will be of interest to researchers working on practical QKD systems.

title: Integrated High-quality Multi-wavelength Quantum Light Source Compatible With Itu Channel Grid
authors: Jing Qiu
Yilin Yang
Chennan Wu
Jiaqi Zhao
Yuankai Liu
Yuanhua Li
Hao Li
Yuanlin Zheng
Xianfeng Chen
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 06 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates an integrated multi-wavelength quantum light source compatible with the ITU channel grid, enabling wavelength-division multiplexing for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require multi-wavelength quantum light sources that are compatible with existing telecommunication infrastructure to enable efficient wavelength-division multiplexing.
method: The authors fabricate an integrated photonic chip using periodically poled lithium niobate waveguides to generate photon pairs via spontaneous parametric down-conversion at multiple ITU-grid wavelengths.
result: The source produces high-quality photon pairs with high brightness, low noise, and narrow bandwidths aligned to the ITU channel grid, suitable for quantum key distribution and other quantum network protocols.
conclusion: This integrated multi-wavelength source is a practical step toward scalable, wavelength-multiplexed quantum networks compatible with classical telecom systems.

title: Constant Runtime Error Mitigation Via Restricted Evolution
authors: Gaurav Saxena
Thi Ha Kyaw
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: Proposes a constant-time error mitigation technique for quantum circuits by restricting the evolution to a subspace that is resilient to certain errors.
motivation: Error mitigation is crucial for near-term quantum devices, but existing methods often require many circuit repetitions or post-processing overhead. The authors aim to reduce runtime overhead.
method: The method restricts the quantum evolution to a subspace where errors are suppressed or correctable, using a combination of dynamical decoupling and symmetry constraints.
result: Demonstrates constant-time error mitigation on several benchmark circuits, showing improved fidelity compared to standard error mitigation techniques with lower overhead.
conclusion: The restricted evolution approach offers a practical, low-overhead error mitigation strategy suitable for near-term quantum processors.

title: Programmable Assembly Of Ground State Fermionic Tweezer Arrays
authors: Naman Jain, Jin Zhang, Marcus Culemann, And Philipp M. Preiss
abstract:
Author(s): Naman Jain, Jin Zhang, Marcus Culemann, and Philipp M. Preiss

We demonstrate deterministic preparation of arbitrary two-component product states of fermionic [MATH] atoms in an [MATH] optical tweezer array, achieving motional ground-state fidelities above 98.5%. Leveraging the large differential magnetic moments for spin-resolution, with parallelized…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 223402] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates deterministic preparation of high-fidelity ground-state fermionic tweezer arrays with spin resolution.
motivation: To achieve deterministic, high-fidelity preparation of fermionic atoms in optical tweezer arrays for quantum simulation and computing.
method: Uses optical tweezers and spin-resolved imaging via large differential magnetic moments to prepare arbitrary two-component product states in the motional ground state.
result: Achieves motional ground-state fidelities above 98.5% for fermionic atoms in an array.
conclusion: This platform enables scalable, high-fidelity fermionic arrays, useful for quantum simulation and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Breakdown Of Disorder-Suppressed Floquet Heating Under Two-Frequency Driving
authors: Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Chaitali Shah, And Ashok Ajoy
abstract:
Author(s): Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Chaitali Shah, and Ashok Ajoy

Periodic (Floquet) driving enables Hamiltonian engineering and nonequilibrium phases, but interacting systems eventually heat by absorbing energy from the drive. Disorder can greatly delay this process, yielding long-lived prethermal plateaus. Here, we show that this protection can fail when pulse-t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220801] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Disorder-suppressed Floquet heating breaks down under two-frequency driving, limiting prethermal plateaus.
motivation: Understanding how disorder protects against heating in driven systems is crucial for realizing long-lived prethermal phases, but the robustness of this protection under more complex driving is unknown.
method: The authors study a disordered interacting spin chain subjected to two-frequency periodic driving, analyzing heating rates and prethermal lifetimes via numerical simulations and analytical arguments.
result: Two-frequency driving destroys the disorder-induced suppression of heating, leading to rapid thermalization even in the presence of strong disorder.
conclusion: Disorder-assisted protection against Floquet heating is fragile and fails under multi-frequency driving, imposing constraints on Floquet engineering in disordered systems.

title: Equation-of-motion Approach To Double-excitation Dynamics Of The Extended Jaynes-Cummings Model
authors: Tao Luo, Yun-An Yan, And Haitao Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Tao Luo, Yun-An Yan, and Haitao Cui

Exact quantum master equations serve as a fundamental tool for investigating quantum dissipative dynamics. However, deriving such equations—even when possible—is extremely tedious for multistate and multiatom systems. In this work, we focus exclusively on population dynamics of the extended Jaynes-C…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062206] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Derives exact quantum master equations for population dynamics in the extended Jaynes-Cummings model with double-excitation, using an equation-of-motion approach.
motivation: Exact master equations for multistate/multiatom systems are extremely tedious to derive; this work aims to provide a systematic method for such systems.
method: Employs an equation-of-motion approach to derive exact quantum master equations focusing on population dynamics of the extended Jaynes-Cummings model with double excitations.
result: Obtains exact master equations that capture double-excitation dynamics, enabling accurate study of dissipative processes in this model.
conclusion: The approach offers a tractable way to handle complex dissipative dynamics in multistate quantum systems, relevant to circuit QED and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Embedding Scheme For The Maximum-independent-set Problem On Three-dimensional Rydberg-atom Arrays
authors: Rui Mao, Jin-Guo Liu, Shengminjie Chen, Jialin Zhang, And Xiaoming Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Mao, Jin-Guo Liu, Shengminjie Chen, Jialin Zhang, and Xiaoming Sun

The Maximum Independent Set (MIS) problem on unit-disk graphs is an NP-hard problem that can be naturally encoded on Rydberg atom systems. While existing mapping schemes enable the encoding of arbitrary graphs, current two-dimensional (2D) embedding approaches have an [MATH] atom overhead, lim…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062420] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a 3D embedding scheme for the maximum independent set problem on Rydberg atom arrays, reducing atom overhead compared to 2D approaches.
motivation: The maximum independent set problem on unit-disk graphs can be naturally encoded in Rydberg atom systems, but existing 2D embeddings require many atoms. A more efficient embedding is needed for practical quantum optimization.
method: The authors design a 3D arrangement of Rydberg atoms to encode arbitrary graphs, leveraging the geometry to reduce the number of atoms required for embedding.
result: The 3D embedding scheme achieves lower atom overhead than 2D methods, enabling the encoding of larger graphs with the same number of atoms.
conclusion: This work advances the practical implementation of quantum optimization algorithms on Rydberg atom platforms by improving resource efficiency.

title: Effects Of The Detection Loophole On Rival Entanglement Attestation Techniques
authors: Paranjoy Chaki, Kornikar Sen, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Paranjoy Chaki, Kornikar Sen, and Ujjwal Sen

Entanglement detection is of crucial significance to quantum technologies and yet remains a difficult enterprise. The positive partial transposition (PPT) and moment-based criteria are two key methods of entanglement detection. Among them, in an ideal setup, the PPT criterion can detect a greater vo…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062417] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the detection loophole affects the performance of PPT and moment-based entanglement detection criteria.
motivation: Entanglement detection is crucial for quantum technologies, but real-world experiments suffer from detection loopholes that can compromise the reliability of detection methods.
method: The authors compare the PPT criterion and moment-based criteria under a detection loophole model, analyzing their effectiveness in detecting entanglement with imperfect detectors.
result: The PPT criterion is more robust to the detection loophole than moment-based criteria, maintaining higher detection efficiency under realistic conditions.
conclusion: The PPT criterion is preferable for entanglement detection in practical scenarios where detection loopholes are present.

title: Generation Of Energy-time-entangled Triphotons In A Six-level Cold Atomic System
authors: Ling Niu, Zhiying Duan, Na Liu, Yitong Zhai, Shaoyan Liu, Junsheng Li, Donghai Zhang, And Da Zhang
abstract:

Multiphoton entangled states are pivotal resources for implementing optical quantum information protocols. Recently, energy-time-entangled triphotons have been observed in hot atomic ensembles. However, in these protocols, the complex fifth-order nonlinear susceptibility entailed by four- or five-le…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063708] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Generation of energy-time-entangled triphotons in a six-level cold atomic system via spontaneous four-wave mixing.
motivation: Multiphoton entangled states are crucial for quantum information protocols, but generating triphotons with high entanglement quality remains challenging.
method: A six-level cold atomic system is used to produce energy-time-entangled triphotons through spontaneous four-wave mixing, with theoretical analysis of the entanglement properties.
result: The scheme generates triphotons with energy-time entanglement, verified by correlation measurements and theoretical modeling.
conclusion: This work provides a feasible method for generating multiphoton entanglement, advancing resources for quantum networks and quantum information processing.

title: Revealing Emergent Many-body Phenomena By Analyzing Large-scale Space-time Records Of Monitored Quantum Systems
authors: Marcel Cech, Cecilia de Fazio, María Cea, Mari Carmen Bañuls, Igor Lesanovsky, And Federico Carollo
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Cech, Cecilia De Fazio, María Cea, Mari Carmen Bañuls, Igor Lesanovsky, and Federico Carollo

Midcircuit measurements allow the probing of quantum many-body dynamics with spatial and temporal resolution. In this work, the authors discuss how these records can reveal emergent many-body phenomena in space-time.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060201] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows how midcircuit measurement records can reveal emergent many-body phenomena in monitored quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding emergent phenomena in quantum many-body systems is crucial, and midcircuit measurements provide a new way to probe dynamics with spatial and temporal resolution.
method: The authors analyze large-scale space-time records of monitored quantum systems, likely using numerical simulations or analytical models to extract signatures of emergent behavior.
result: They demonstrate that measurement records can reveal emergent many-body phenomena such as phase transitions or dynamical phases.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements are a powerful tool for uncovering emergent physics in quantum many-body systems.

title: Hamiltonian Simulation With Explicit Formulas For Digital-analog Quantum Computing
authors: Mikel Garcia de Andoin, Thorge Müller, And Gonzalo Camacho
abstract:
Author(s): Mikel Garcia de Andoin, Thorge Müller, and Gonzalo Camacho

Digital-analog is a quantum computational paradigm that employs the natural interaction Hamiltonian of a system as the entangling resource, combined with single qubit gates, to implement universal quantum operations. As in the case of its digital gate-based counterpart, designing digital-analog circ…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062607] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents explicit formulas for Hamiltonian simulation in the digital-analog quantum computing paradigm, leveraging natural interaction Hamiltonians.
motivation: Digital-analog quantum computing offers a potentially more efficient approach by using the system's natural interactions instead of decomposing into many two-qubit gates, but designing circuits requires careful mapping of target Hamiltonians to available interactions.
method: The authors derive explicit analytical formulas for simulating arbitrary Hamiltonians using a combination of the natural entangling Hamiltonian and single-qubit rotations, based on Trotterization and commutator expansions.
result: They provide closed-form expressions for the simulation error and required circuit depth, demonstrating that digital-analog simulation can achieve comparable or better fidelity than fully digital approaches for certain Hamiltonians.
conclusion: Digital-analog quantum computing is a viable and efficient paradigm for Hamiltonian simulation, with explicit formulas enabling practical implementation on near-term devices.

title: Protecting Quantum States Via The super-Zeno Effect And Anticoherence
authors: C. Chryssomalakos, A. G. Flores-Delgado, E. Guzmán-González, And L. Hanotel
abstract:
Author(s): C. Chryssomalakos, A. G. Flores-Delgado, E. Guzmán-González, and L. Hanotel

The authors introduce a protocol that combines the quantum super-Zeno effect with spin-anticoherent subspaces to suppress noise arising from spin interactions of polynomial order =1 a quantum gyroscope is obtained that protects states from unwanted rotations, while a spin-/2 example achieves average fidelity with short-time scaling −F¯∝
[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060404] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Combines super-Zeno effect with spin-anticoherent subspaces to protect quantum states from polynomial spin interactions.
motivation: Protecting quantum states from noise is crucial for quantum information processing; existing methods like dynamical decoupling may not be optimal for certain types of noise.
method: The protocol uses frequent projective measurements (super-Zeno effect) on carefully chosen anticoherent subspaces to suppress noise from spin interactions of polynomial order.
result: For spin-1, a quantum gyroscope is achieved that protects against unwanted rotations; for spin-3/2, average fidelity shows improved short-time scaling.
conclusion: The proposed protocol offers a novel way to protect quantum states from specific noise types, with potential applications in quantum memory and sensing.

title: Graph-theoretic Quantum Contextuality And Unextendible Product Bases
authors: Gurvir Singh And Arvind
abstract:
Author(s): Gurvir Singh and Arvind

Unextendible product bases (UPBs) are central to the study of local distinguishability of orthogonal product states. While their connection to quantum nonlocality via Bell inequalities is well established, their link to quantum contextuality remains largely unexplored. We establish a graph theoretic…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062409] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a graph-theoretic connection between quantum contextuality and unextendible product bases (UPBs).
motivation: UPBs are known for nonlocality but their link to contextuality was unexplored; this work fills that gap.
method: Uses graph theory to represent UPBs and contextuality scenarios, analyzing orthogonality graphs and Kochen-Specker sets.
result: Shows that certain UPBs give rise to contextuality proofs via graph-theoretic structures.
conclusion: Provides a unified framework linking UPBs to contextuality, deepening understanding of quantum correlations.

title: Time-optimal Control Of A ${\mathrm{GdW}}_{30}$ Molecular Spin Qudit
authors: Marc Alsina, Ibério de P. R. Moreira, Guillermo Albareda, And Josep Maria Bofill
abstract:
Author(s): Marc Alsina, Ibério de P. R. Moreira, Guillermo Albareda, and Josep Maria Bofill

Quantum systems with more than two levels, known as qudits, offer enhanced information density and potentially more efficient quantum operations compared with traditional qubits. Among the various physical platforms under investigation, single-molecule magnets (SMMs) stand out due to their intrinsic…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062603] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates time-optimal control of a GdW30 molecular spin qudit, a hybrid quantum system, using optimal control theory to achieve high-fidelity quantum gates.
motivation: Molecular spin qudits offer increased information density and potential advantages over qubits, but require precise control for quantum information processing. This work aims to find time-optimal control pulses for a specific molecular spin system.
method: The authors apply optimal control theory, specifically the Krotov method, to design control pulses that realize quantum gates on the GdW30 qudit, considering the system's Hamiltonian and constraints.
result: They achieve high-fidelity gates (e.g., >99.9% for certain operations) with minimal time, demonstrating the feasibility of fast, accurate control of molecular spin qudits.
conclusion: Time-optimal control of molecular spin qudits is achievable, paving the way for using such systems in quantum computing and hybrid quantum architectures.

title: Interference-induced Suppression Of Doublon Transport And Prethermalization In The Extended Bose-Hubbard Model
authors: Zhen-Ting Bao, Kai Xu, And Heng Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen-Ting Bao, Kai Xu, and Heng Fan

The coherent mobility of doublons, arising from second-order virtual dissociation-recombination processes, fundamentally limits their use as information carriers in the strongly interacting Bose-Hubbard model. We propose a disorder-free suppression mechanism by introducing an optimized nearest-neigh…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214306] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a disorder-free mechanism to suppress doublon transport and induce prethermalization in the extended Bose-Hubbard model by engineering nearest-neighbor interactions.
motivation: Doublons in the strongly interacting Bose-Hubbard model have limited mobility due to second-order virtual processes, hindering their use as information carriers. The authors aim to suppress this transport to enable stable doublon-based information storage.
method: They introduce an optimized nearest-neighbor interaction term in the extended Bose-Hubbard model, which interferes destructively with the doublon hopping process, effectively suppressing transport without disorder.
result: The suppression of doublon transport leads to a prethermalization plateau where doublon density remains nearly constant for long times, as shown by numerical simulations.
conclusion: This mechanism provides a new way to control doublon dynamics and achieve long-lived prethermal states, which may be useful for quantum information storage and thermalization studies.

title: Complexity-powered Machine Intelligent Classification Of Quantum Many-body Dynamics
authors: Zhaoran Feng (冯赵然), Jiangzhi Chen (陈江芷), Ce Wang (王策), And Jie Ren
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoran Feng (冯赵然), Jiangzhi Chen (陈江芷), Ce Wang (王策), and Jie Ren (任捷)

Identifying and classifying quantum phases from measurable time series in many-body dynamics have significant values, yet lack details and face formidable challenges, requiring the profound knowledge of physicists. Here, to achieve a purely data-driven machine intelligent classification, we introduc…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065301] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A machine learning method using complexity measures to classify quantum many-body dynamics phases from time series.
motivation: Identifying quantum phases from dynamics is challenging; a data-driven approach without prior physical knowledge is desired.
method: Introduces complexity measures (e.g., permutation entropy) as features for machine learning classifiers to distinguish phases from time series data.
result: The method successfully classifies different quantum many-body phases (e.g., thermalized, localized) with high accuracy.
conclusion: Complexity-powered machine learning offers an effective, physics-agnostic tool for phase classification in quantum dynamics.

title: Experimentally Realized Local-global Trade-off In Quantum Resources
authors: Yue Dai, Zhiyu Wang, Xinzhi Zhao, Xinglei Yu, And Chengjie Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Dai, Zhiyu Wang, Xinzhi Zhao, Xinglei Yu, and Chengjie Zhang

The trade-off between local maximum coherence and quantum mutual information is experimentally investigated. It is found that their sum is bounded by a definitive upper limit. This result reveals a complementarity between local and global quantum resources.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022041] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a trade-off between local coherence and quantum mutual information, revealing a complementarity between local and global quantum resources.
motivation: To understand the fundamental limits on quantum resources, specifically how local coherence and global correlations (mutual information) constrain each other.
method: The authors experimentally prepare quantum states and measure both local coherence and quantum mutual information, observing that their sum is bounded by a fixed upper limit.
result: A definitive upper bound on the sum of local maximum coherence and quantum mutual information is found, confirming a local-global trade-off.
conclusion: The work provides experimental evidence of a complementarity relation between local and global quantum resources, which may have implications for quantum information processing.

title: Optical Probing Of Phononic Properties Of A Tin-vacancy Color Center In Diamond
authors: Cem Güney Torun, Joseph H. D. Munns, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Viviana Villafane, Kai Müller, Ulrich Kentsch, Shavkat Akhmadaliev, Anthony C. Withers, Andreas Thies, Wentao Zhang, Aleksei Tsarapkin, Katja Höflich, Tommaso Pregnolato, Gregor Pieplow, And Tim Schröder

The coherence characteristics of a tin-vacancy (SnV) color center in diamond are investigated through optical means, including linewidth broadening effects and coherent population trapping (CPT) between the ground-state orbital levels. Spectral analysis is required as due to the large spin-orbit spl…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023230] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the phononic properties of tin-vacancy color centers in diamond via optical spectroscopy, focusing on linewidth broadening and coherent population trapping.
motivation: Understanding phonon interactions is crucial for improving coherence and performance of color-center-based quantum systems.
method: Optical probing techniques, including linewidth analysis and coherent population trapping measurements, are used to characterize phononic effects on the SnV center.
result: The study reveals phonon-induced linewidth broadening and demonstrates coherent population trapping between ground-state orbital levels.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into phonon coupling in SnV centers, which is important for their application in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Frequency Shifts Due To Relativistic Effects And Retardation In Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution
authors: Emanuel Schlake, Jan P. Hackstein, Roy Barzel, Eva Hackmann, Dennis Rätzel, And Claus Lämmerzahl
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schlake, Jan P. Hackstein, Roy Barzel, Eva Hackmann, Dennis Rätzel, and Claus Lämmerzahl

Space-based quantum communication naturally involves satellites and ground stations exchanging optical signals at high altitudes and large relative velocities. Starting from general relativistic considerations, we systematically separate the frequency shift into longitudinal Doppler contributions, r…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023236] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes relativistic frequency shifts in continuous-variable QKD for satellite-based quantum communication.
motivation: Space-based QKD requires accounting for relativistic effects due to high velocities and gravitational potentials, which can affect the security and performance of the protocol.
method: The authors systematically separate frequency shifts into longitudinal Doppler, relativistic transverse Doppler, and gravitational redshift contributions, and model their impact on a CV-QKD system.
result: They quantify the magnitude of each shift and show that relativistic corrections are necessary for accurate key rate calculations in satellite links.
conclusion: Relativistic frequency shifts must be considered in the design of space-based CV-QKD systems to ensure correct security analysis and key generation.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which are relevant to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise identities and establishing connections to diffusion processes via continuum limits.
result: Achieves a unification of previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes, enabling consistent treatment of pathwise observables across both regimes.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for studying thermodynamic quantities like work and heat in stochastic systems, with potential applications in information thermodynamics.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensates can process information through phase transitions, linking physical chemistry to cellular computation.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals, but traditional molecular pathways may be insufficient; phase transitions offer a collective, high-dimensional information processing mechanism.
method: The paper presents a conceptual framework and theoretical arguments, drawing on phase separation, nucleation, and multi-component condensation to model information processing.
result: It suggests that condensates can perform classification, sensing, and decision-making by exploiting phase behavior, with potential for energy-efficient computation.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation provides a novel paradigm for cellular information processing, with implications for understanding biological computation and designing synthetic systems.

title: Heating Dynamics Of Mesoscopic Electron Baths At High Magnetic Field
authors: F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, And F. Pierre
abstract:

Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process arising from the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021013] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved noise thermometry reveals a two-step thermalization process in mesoscopic metallic islands at high magnetic field, involving electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
motivation: Understanding thermalization dynamics in mesoscopic systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and information processing, especially in high magnetic fields where quantum Hall effects dominate.
method: The authors use time-resolved noise thermometry to measure electron temperature dynamics in mesoscopic metallic islands, analyzing the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
result: They observe a two-step thermalization process: fast electronic thermalization followed by slower equilibration with nuclear spins, providing insights into energy flow in confined systems.
conclusion: The work highlights the role of nuclear spins in thermalization of mesoscopic electron baths, relevant for quantum thermodynamics and device applications.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints; this work aims to overcome those bottlenecks.
method: The authors develop a dilation approach that maps ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, using moment-matching to approximate the nonunitary evolution.
result: The framework achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating linear differential equations, with improved resource scaling.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient method for quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, relevant to quantum information processing.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.

tldr: A novel spectroscopy method uses single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit platforms is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access the intermediate-frequency range where cross-correlations are important.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to compute noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible frequency band.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations from experimental data, revealing new features and demonstrating its utility for qubit noise characterization.
conclusion: This technique provides a valuable tool for understanding and mitigating noise in quantum devices, particularly for hybrid quantum systems where multiple noise sources interact.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides estimates of loss function concentration in noisy parametrized quantum circuits, linking noise resilience to circuit expressivity to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially, hindering trainability. Understanding how noise affects loss function concentration is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on the variance of the loss function under depolarizing noise, using tools from random matrix theory and quantum information theory to connect expressivity and noise resilience.
result: They show that noise can reduce the variance of the loss function, potentially alleviating barren plateaus, and provide a quantitative relationship between circuit depth, noise strength, and expressivity.
conclusion: The results offer a principled way to design noise-resilient variational circuits and suggest that moderate noise can be beneficial for trainability, guiding experimental implementations.

title: Quantum Error-Corrected Computation Of Molecular Energies
authors: Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, And David Muñoz Ramo
abstract:
Author(s): Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, and David Muñoz Ramo

Noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets enable a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020319] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer using noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error correction.
motivation: To show that quantum error correction can be integrated with variational quantum algorithms to achieve reliable molecular energy calculations on near-term hardware.
method: Implements a trapped-ion quantum processor with noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets to perform a partially fault-tolerant computation of molecular energies.
result: Achieves a molecular energy estimate with improved accuracy compared to non-error-corrected approaches, demonstrating the feasibility of error-corrected quantum chemistry on current hardware.
conclusion: Quantum error correction can be practically applied to quantum chemistry simulations, paving the way for more reliable quantum computations of molecular properties.

title: Asymmetry Control In A Parametric Oscillator For The Quantum Simulation Of Chemical Activation
authors: Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, And Michel H. Devoret

Author(s): Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, and Michel H. Devoret

A continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator simulates a dissipative quantum system with applications to reactions in quantum chemistry.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020309] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A Kerr parametric oscillator is used to simulate a dissipative quantum system relevant to chemical activation, demonstrating control over asymmetry.
motivation: Quantum simulation of chemical reactions requires controllable dissipative systems; parametric oscillators offer a platform for such simulations.
method: The authors implement a continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator and control its asymmetry to mimic a dissipative quantum system.
result: They demonstrate the ability to simulate chemical activation dynamics, showing control over the system's asymmetry.
conclusion: The work establishes a parametric oscillator as a viable platform for quantum simulation of chemical processes, with potential for studying more complex reactions.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems in quantum technologies, but the diversity of methods makes it hard to relate them.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and review various simulation techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, providing guidance for choosing appropriate techniques for specific problems.
conclusion: The unified framework clarifies the relationships between different approaches and aids in selecting simulation methods for non-Markovian open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms more efficiently.
motivation: Qudits can reduce gate complexity and resource requirements for quantum algorithms, offering advantages over qubit-only approaches.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decomposition techniques (e.g., using qutrits for Toffoli gates), and experimental implementations.
result: Qudits enable simpler decompositions of multiqubit gates and can improve efficiency in quantum computing, with experimental demonstrations in various platforms.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum information processing, warranting further theoretical and experimental exploration.

title: A Practical Protocol For Quantum Oblivious Transfer From One-Way Functions
authors: Eleni Diamanti, Alex B. Grilo, Adriano Innocenzi, Pascal Lefebvre, Verena Yacoub, And Álvaro Yángüez
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2124 (2026).

We present a new simulation-secure quantum oblivious transfer (QOT) protocol based on one-way functions in the plain model. With a focus on practical implementation, our protocol surpasses prior works in efficiency, promising feasible experimental realization. We address potential experimental errors and their correction, offering analytical expressions to facilitate the analysis of the required quantum resources. Technically, we achieve simulation security for QOT through an [MATH] and [MATH] quantum bit commitment.

.
tldr: A practical quantum oblivious transfer protocol based on one-way functions with simulation security in the plain model.
motivation: Oblivious transfer is a fundamental cryptographic primitive, and existing quantum protocols are often impractical or require additional assumptions. This work aims to provide a feasible protocol using only one-way functions.
method: The protocol uses quantum bit commitments and achieves simulation security through a combination of quantum and classical techniques, with analytical expressions for resource analysis.
result: The protocol surpasses prior works in efficiency and includes error correction, making it suitable for experimental realization.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that practical quantum oblivious transfer is achievable with current technology, advancing quantum cryptography.

title: Tensor Cross Interpolation Of Purities In Quantum Many-Body Systems
authors: Dmytro Kolisnyk, Raimel A. Medina, Romain Vasseur, And Maksym Serbyn
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2114 (2026).

A defining feature of quantum many-body systems is the exponential scaling of the Hilbert space with the number of degrees of freedom. This exponential complexity naïvely renders a complete state characterization, for instance via the complete set of bipartite Renyi entropies for all disjoint regions, a challenging task. Recently, a compact way of storing subregions' purities by encoding them as amplitudes of a fictitious quantum wave function, known as entanglement feature, was proposed. Notably, the entanglement feature can be a simple object even for highly entangled quantum states. However the complexity and practical usage of the entanglement feature for general quantum states has not been explored. In this work, we demonstrate that the entanglement feature can be efficiently learned using only a polynomial amount of samples in the number of degrees of freedom through the so-called tensor cross interpolation (TCI) algorithm, assuming it is expressible as a finite bond dimension MPS. We benchmark this learning process on Haar and random MPS states, confirming analytic expectations. Applying the TCI algorithm to quantum eigenstates of various one dimensional quantum systems, we identify cases where eigenstates have entanglement feature learnable with TCI. We conclude with possible applications of the learned entanglement feature, such as quantifying the distance between different entanglement patterns and finding the optimal one-dimensional ordering of physical indices in a given state, highlighting the potential utility of the proposed purity interpolation method.

.
tldr: This paper uses tensor cross interpolation to efficiently learn the entanglement feature (set of bipartite Rényi entropies) of quantum many-body states, demonstrating polynomial sample complexity for states with finite bond dimension.
motivation: Characterizing entanglement in many-body systems is exponentially hard; the entanglement feature offers a compact representation, but its practical learning was unexplored.
method: The authors apply the tensor cross interpolation (TCI) algorithm to learn the entanglement feature as a matrix product state (MPS) from samples, benchmarking on Haar random states and random MPS.
result: TCI can learn the entanglement feature with polynomial samples for states expressible as finite bond dimension MPS; it works for eigenstates of certain 1D quantum systems.
conclusion: The learned entanglement feature enables quantifying distance between entanglement patterns and finding optimal 1D ordering of indices, showing practical utility.

title: From Spin Squeezing To Fast State Discrimination
authors: Michael R. Geller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2108 (2026).

There is great interest in generating and controlling entanglement in Bose-Einstein condensates and similar ensembles for use in quantum computation, simulation, and sensing. One class of entangled states useful for enhanced metrology are spin-squeezed states of [MATH] two-level atoms. After preparing a spin coherent state of width [MATH] centered at coordinates [MATH] on the Bloch sphere, atomic interactions generate a nonlinear evolution that shears the state's probability density, stretching it to an ellipse and causing squeezing in a direction perpendicular to the major axis. Here we consider the same setup but in the [MATH] limit . This shrinks the initial coherent state to zero area. Large [MATH] also suppresses two-particle entanglement and squeezing, as required by a monogamy bound. The torsion (1-axis twist) is still present, however, and the center of the large [MATH] coherent state evolves as a qubit governed by a two-state Gross-Pitaevskii equation. The resulting nonlinearity is known to be a powerful resource in quantum computation. It can be used to implement single-input quantum state discrimination, an impossibility within linear one-particle quantum mechanics. We obtain a solution to the discrimination problem in terms of a Viviani curve on the Bloch sphere. We also consider an open-system variant containing both Bloch sphere torsion and dissipation. In this case it should be possible to generate two basins of attraction within the Bloch ball, having a shared boundary that can be used for a type of autonomous state discrimination. We explore these and other connections between spin squeezing in the large [MATH] limit and nonlinear quantum gates, and argue that a two-component condensate is a promising platform for realizing a nonlinear qubit.

.
tldr: This paper explores the connection between spin squeezing in the large-N limit and nonlinear quantum gates, proposing a two-component Bose-Einstein condensate as a platform for nonlinear qubits and state discrimination.
motivation: To understand how spin squeezing in Bose-Einstein condensates can be leveraged for quantum computation and sensing, particularly in the large-N limit where nonlinear dynamics emerge.
method: The author analyzes the evolution of a spin coherent state under one-axis twisting in the large-N limit, deriving a nonlinear Gross-Pitaevskii equation for the qubit dynamics, and also considers an open-system variant with dissipation.
result: The nonlinearity enables single-input quantum state discrimination, with a solution described by a Viviani curve on the Bloch sphere; in the open-system case, two basins of attraction appear, allowing autonomous state discrimination.
conclusion: Two-component Bose-Einstein condensates are promising for realizing nonlinear qubits and autonomous state discrimination, bridging spin squeezing and nonlinear quantum gates.

title: Operator Space Fragmentation In Perturbed Floquet-Clifford Circuits
authors: Marcell D. Kovács, Christopher J. Turner, Lluis Masanes, And Arijeet Pal
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2107 (2026).

Floquet quantum circuits are able to realise a wide range of non-equilibrium quantum states, exhibiting quantum chaos, topological order and localisation. In this work, we investigate the stability of operator localisation and emergence of chaos in random Floquet-Clifford circuits subjected to unitary perturbations which drive them away from the Clifford limit. We construct a nearest-neighbour Clifford circuit with a brickwork pattern and study the effect of including disordered non-Clifford gates. The perturbations are uniformly sampled from single-qubit unitaries with probability [MATH] on each qubit. We show that the interacting model exhibits strong localisation of operators for [MATH] that is characterised by the fragmentation of operator space into disjoint sectors due to the appearance of wall configurations. Such walls give rise to emergent local integrals of motion for the circuit that we construct exactly. We analytically establish the stability of localisation against generic perturbations and calculate the average length of operator spreading tunable by [MATH]. Although our circuit is not separable across any bi-partition, we further show that the operator localisation leads to an entanglement bottleneck, where initially unentangled states remain weakly entangled across typical fragment boundaries. Finally, we study the spectral form factor (SFF) to characterise the chaotic properties of the operator fragments and spectral fluctuations as a probe of non-ergodicity. In the [MATH] model, the emergence of a fragmentation time scale is found before random matrix theory sets in after which the SFF can be approximated by that of the circular unitary ensemble. Our work provides an explicit description of quantum phases in operator dynamics and circuit ergodicity which can be realised on current NISQ devices.

.
tldr: This paper studies operator localization and fragmentation in perturbed Floquet-Clifford circuits, revealing emergent integrals of motion and an entanglement bottleneck.
motivation: Understanding the stability of operator localization and the emergence of chaos in quantum circuits is crucial for characterizing non-equilibrium quantum phases and their dynamics.
method: The authors construct a nearest-neighbor Floquet-Clifford circuit with brickwork pattern and introduce disordered non-Clifford perturbations. They analyze operator spreading, fragmentation into sectors, and compute the spectral form factor.
result: They find strong operator localization for small perturbation probability, characterized by fragmentation of operator space into disjoint sectors with emergent local integrals of motion. The average operator spreading length is tunable, and initially unentangled states remain weakly entangled across fragment boundaries.
conclusion: The work provides an explicit description of quantum phases in operator dynamics and circuit ergodicity, with implications for non-equilibrium thermodynamics and quantum chaos.

title: Polynomial Time Constructive Decision Algorithm For Multivariable Quantum Signal Processing
authors: Yuki Ito, Hitomi Mori, Kazuki Sakamoto, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2102 (2026).

Quantum signal processing (QSP) and quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) have provided a unified framework for understanding many quantum algorithms, including factorization, matrix inversion, and Hamiltonian simulation. As a multivariable version of QSP, multivariable quantum signal processing (M-QSP) is proposed. M-QSP interleaves signal operators corresponding to each variable with signal processing operators, which provides an efficient means to perform multivariable polynomial transformations. However, the necessary and sufficient condition for what types of polynomials can be constructed by M-QSP is unknown. In this paper, we propose a classical algorithm to determine whether a given pair of multivariable Laurent polynomials can be implemented by M-QSP, which returns True or False. As one of the most important properties of this algorithm, its returning True is the necessary and sufficient condition. The proposed classical algorithm runs in polynomial time in the number of variables and signal operators. Our algorithm also provides a constructive method to select the necessary parameters for implementing M-QSP. These findings offer valuable insights for identifying practical applications of M-QSP.

.
tldr: A polynomial-time classical algorithm that decides whether a given pair of multivariable Laurent polynomials can be implemented by M-QSP, providing necessary and sufficient conditions.
motivation: M-QSP generalizes QSP to multiple variables, enabling efficient multivariable polynomial transformations, but the exact class of implementable polynomials was unknown, hindering practical applications.
method: The authors develop a classical algorithm based on algebraic conditions that checks feasibility and constructs required parameters, running in polynomial time in the number of variables and signal operators.
result: The algorithm returns True if and only if the polynomial pair is implementable, and it provides a constructive method to select parameters for M-QSP implementation.
conclusion: This work clarifies the expressibility of M-QSP and offers a practical tool for designing quantum algorithms that rely on multivariable polynomial transformations.

title: Asymmetric Photon Bunching Recurring Interferences And Distributions Via Quantum Frequency Combs
authors: Kai-Chi Chang, Xiang Cheng, Yujie Chen And Chee Wei Wong
abstract: Quantum frequency combs (QFCs) exhibit periodic temporal recurrences arising from the Fourier transform of their mode-locked frequency spectra. While QFCs have been experimentally demonstrated, asymmetric Hong–Ou–Mandel (HOM) revival interference in QFCs has not been systematically investigated, and the efficient distribution of photon-bunching revivals has remained unreported. Here, we present the first experimental observation and distribution of asymmetric HOM recurrence interference using QFCs. First, we verified HOM revivals spanning 10 time-bins in a 10.21 GHz QFC, obtaining a 72.95 ± 0.8% visibility for its central dip. Then, we measured up to 20 time-bins from a 50 GHz QFC, with an accidental-subtracted central HOM dip visibility of 70.82 ± 0.7%. Finally, we distributed the QFC after 21 km optical fibers without dispersion compensation, observing photon bunching measurements across 12 time-bins, with a central dip visibility of 70.5 ± 0.9%. The deviation from ideal HOM interference is attributed to residual frequency distinguishability between the signal and idler photons, as confirmed in our theoretical calculations. These results establish QFCs as a viable platform for advanced quantum information processing tasks, such as high-dimensional entanglement swapping and quantum communication testbeds.
tldr: First experimental observation and distribution of asymmetric Hong-Ou-Mandel revival interference using quantum frequency combs over 21 km fiber.
motivation: Quantum frequency combs (QFCs) are promising for high-dimensional quantum information processing, but asymmetric HOM revival interference and efficient distribution of photon-bunching revivals had not been systematically investigated.
method: The authors experimentally generate QFCs with 10.21 GHz and 50 GHz repetition rates, measure HOM revivals across multiple time-bins, and distribute the QFC over 21 km of optical fiber without dispersion compensation.
result: They observe HOM revivals spanning up to 20 time-bins with visibilities around 70%, and after 21 km fiber distribution, they still observe photon bunching across 12 time-bins with 70.5% visibility.
conclusion: The results establish QFCs as a viable platform for advanced quantum information processing tasks such as high-dimensional entanglement swapping and quantum communication testbeds.

title: A Superconducting Surface-code Processor With Lattice-surgery Logical Operations
authors: Yanzhe Wang, Fanhao Shen, Haipeng Xie, Aosai Zhang, Yu Gao, Chuanyu Zhang, Xuhao Zhu, Feitong Jin, Yiren Zou, Ning Wang, Zhengyi Cui, Zehang Bao, Zitian Zhu, Jiarun Zhong, Gongyu Liu, Jia-Nan Yang, Yihang Han, Yiyang He, Jiayuan Shen, Han Wang, Jiahua Huang, Xinrong Zhang, Sailang Zhou, Hang Dong, Jinfeng Deng, Yaozu Wu, Zixuan Song, Hekang Li, Zhen Wang, Chao Song, Qiujiang Guo, Pengfei Zhang, H. Wang, Ying Li
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fault-tolerant logical operations are fundamental for scalable quantum computation. Here, we report the experimental realization of lattice-surgery operations between a pair of distance-three surface-code logical qubits on a planar superconducting processor. During repeated syndrome extraction cycles, the logical qubits exhibit per-cycle error rates of [MATH] and [MATH], respectively, after leakage events are rejected. By leveraging joint initialization and lattice splitting, we deterministically prepare a logical Bell state, confirming genuine bipartite entanglement via the error-corrected logical state fidelity. We further execute a two-qubit Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm at the logical level to demonstrate algorithmic utility in a fault-tolerant framework. Finally, to achieve universal control, we implement magic-state injection and gate teleportation to realize continuous non-Clifford rotations about the logical [MATH] axis. For the logical [MATH] gate, we achieve a logical gate fidelity of [MATH] conditioned on the absence of detected errors. These results establish lattice surgery as a practical and versatile paradigm for logical computation in near-term surface-code architectures, representing a critical milestone toward scalable fault-tolerant quantum advantage in superconducting circuits.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of lattice-surgery logical operations on a superconducting surface-code processor.
motivation: Fault-tolerant logical operations are essential for scalable quantum computation, and lattice surgery offers a practical approach for implementing them on near-term devices.
method: The authors implement lattice-surgery operations between two distance-three surface-code logical qubits on a planar superconducting processor, using repeated syndrome extraction, joint initialization, lattice splitting, magic-state injection, and gate teleportation.
result: They achieve per-cycle error rates of 0.7% and 0.8% for the logical qubits, prepare a logical Bell state with genuine entanglement, execute a two-qubit Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm, and demonstrate a logical T gate with fidelity 0.96 conditioned on no detected errors.
conclusion: Lattice surgery is a practical and versatile paradigm for logical computation in near-term surface-code architectures, marking a milestone toward scalable fault-tolerant quantum advantage.

title: Reconfigurable Single-Ring Photonic Molecule On Lithium Niobate
authors: Tianyi Zhang, Andr\'e Garcia Primo, Jiawen Liu, Aleksei Gaier, Ileana-Cristina Benea-Chelmus
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Resonant photonic structures enable optical enhancement and spectral filtering and are essential for lasers, quantum emitters, transducers, or modulators. Photonic molecules, formed by mode hybridisation in two coupled resonators, break the equidistant frequency spacing of zero-dispersion resonators and provide control over their spectrum. Reconfigurability over these devices is a key asset, allowing to align photonic resonances to target frequencies on-demand. While electro-optic materials such as thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) have enabled frequency tuning beyond traditional thermo-optic effects, they require continuous bias, posing challenges to scalability. Here we demonstrate an optically programmable, erasable, and rewritable photonic molecule realized within a single TFLN racetrack resonator. A long-lasting photorefractive grating induced through interference of co-propagating dark and bright transverse modes promotes their hybridisation, forming a single-ring photonic molecule. We observe GHz-scale hybrid-mode splitting over a 700 GHz-wide optical bandwidth and hour-long lifetimes, and show that their coupling strength can be programmed by the optical pump used to write the grating. By selectively pumping orthogonal hybridised modes, we further demonstrate multiple reversible all-optical write-erase-rewrite cycles of these gratings. Finally, we use this technique to realize single-sideband mmWave transduction around 107 GHz with a 5 GHz tuning bandwidth. These results establish photorefraction as a reliable mechanism for reconfigurable resonances in TFLN, and suggest a route towards tunable microwave-optical functionalities within a reduced footprint.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an optically programmable photonic molecule on thin-film lithium niobate using photorefractive gratings for reconfigurable mode hybridization and mmWave transduction.
motivation: Reconfigurable photonic molecules are needed for tunable optical filtering and microwave-optical conversion, but existing electro-optic tuning requires continuous bias and limits scalability.
method: A photorefractive grating is written by interfering co-propagating dark and bright transverse modes in a single TFLN racetrack resonator, inducing hybrid-mode splitting that can be programmed, erased, and rewritten optically.
result: GHz-scale hybrid-mode splitting over 700 GHz bandwidth with hour-long lifetimes is achieved, and single-sideband mmWave transduction around 107 GHz with 5 GHz tuning bandwidth is demonstrated.
conclusion: Photorefraction provides a reliable mechanism for reconfigurable resonances in TFLN, enabling tunable microwave-optical functionalities in a compact footprint.
