title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying approaches for complex systems in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex phenomena, but existing methods are diverse and fragmented; a unified framework is needed.
method: The authors review field-theoretic techniques (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism, path integrals) to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review shows how field theories provide a systematic way to compute correlation functions and effective dynamics for these systems.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful and unifying approach for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across disciplines.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials for novel functionalities.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, including time-resolved spectroscopy and dynamical mean-field theory.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable phases, and nonthermal orders like superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation offers a powerful route to engineer quantum states in Mott insulators, with potential for future technologies.

title: On The Dynamical Lie Algebras Of Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithms
authors: Jonathan Allcock, Miklos Santha, Pei Yuan, And Shengyu Zhang
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2119 (2026).

Dynamical Lie algebras (DLAs) have emerged as a valuable tool in the study of parameterized quantum circuits, helping to characterize both their expressiveness and trainability. In particular, the absence or presence of barren plateaus (BPs) – flat regions in parameter space that prevent the efficient training of variational quantum algorithms – has recently been shown to be intimately related to quantities derived from the associated DLA. In this work, we investigate DLAs for the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA), one of the most studied variational quantum algorithms for solving graph MaxCut and other combinatorial optimization problems. While DLAs for QAOA circuits have been studied before, existing results have either been based on numerical evidence, or else correspond to DLA generators specifically chosen to be universal for quantum computation on a subspace of states. We initiate an analytical study of barren plateaus and other statistics of QAOA algorithms, and give bounds on the dimensions of the corresponding DLAs and their centers for general graphs. We then focus on the [MATH]-vertex cycle and complete graphs. For the cycle graph we give an explicit basis, identify its decomposition into the direct sum of a [MATH]-dimensional center and a semisimple component isomorphic to [MATH] copies of [MATH]. We give an explicit basis for this isomorphism, and a closed-form expression for the variance of the cost function, proving the absence of BPs. For the complete graph we prove that the dimension of the DLA is [MATH] and give an explicit basis for the DLA.

.
tldr: This paper analytically studies dynamical Lie algebras (DLAs) for QAOA circuits, providing bounds on DLA dimensions and proving absence of barren plateaus for cycle graphs.
motivation: Understanding the expressiveness and trainability of variational quantum algorithms is crucial for their practical use; DLAs offer a theoretical tool to characterize barren plateaus.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on DLA dimensions for general graphs and explicitly compute DLAs for cycle and complete graphs using Lie algebra decomposition.
result: For cycle graphs, the DLA decomposes into a center and semisimple part, and the cost function variance is computed, proving no barren plateaus. For complete graphs, the DLA dimension is n-1.
conclusion: The work provides rigorous analytical results on QAOA DLAs, but the focus on combinatorial optimization and variational algorithms is not a core interest in quantum information theory.

title: Fully Optimised Variational Simulation Of A Dynamical Quantum Phase Transition On A Trapped-ion Quantum Computer
authors: Lesley Gover, Vinul Wimalaweera, Fariha Azad, Matthew Decross, Michael Foss-Feig, And Andrew G. Green
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2109 (2026).

We time-evolve a translationally invariant quantum state on the Quantinuum H1-1 trapped-ion quantum processor, studying the dynamical quantum phase transition of the transverse field Ising model. This physics requires a delicate cancellation of phases in the many-body wavefunction and presents a tough challenge for current quantum devices. We follow the dynamics using a quantum circuit matrix product state ansatz, optimised for the time-evolution using a fidelity cost function. Sampling costs are mitigated by using the measured values of this circuit as stochastic corrections to a simple classical extrapolation of the ansatz parameters. Our results demonstrate the feasibility of variational quantum time-evolution and reveal a hitherto hidden simplicity of the evolution of the transverse-field Ising model through the dynamical quantum phase transition.

.
tldr: This paper uses a trapped-ion quantum processor to simulate a dynamical quantum phase transition in the transverse field Ising model using a variational quantum circuit matrix product state ansatz.
motivation: Dynamical quantum phase transitions are challenging to simulate on current quantum devices due to the need for delicate phase cancellations. The authors aim to demonstrate the feasibility of variational quantum time-evolution for such problems.
method: They implement a quantum circuit matrix product state ansatz optimized via a fidelity cost function on the Quantinuum H1-1 trapped-ion processor. Sampling costs are mitigated by using measured circuit values as stochastic corrections to a classical extrapolation of ansatz parameters.
result: The variational approach successfully follows the dynamics and reveals a hidden simplicity in the evolution of the transverse-field Ising model through the dynamical quantum phase transition.
conclusion: The results demonstrate that variational quantum time-evolution is feasible on current trapped-ion hardware for simulating complex many-body dynamics.

title: The Complexity Of Local Stoquastic Hamiltonians On 2d Lattices
authors: Gabriel Waite And Michael J. Bremner
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2097 (2026).

We show the 2-Local Stoquastic Hamiltonian problem on a 2D square qubit lattice is StoqMA-complete. We achieve this by extending the spatially sparse circuit construction of Oliveira and Terhal, as well as the perturbative gadgets of Bravyi, DiVincenzo, Oliveira, and Terhal. Our main contributions demonstrate StoqMA circuits can be made spatially sparse and that geometrical, stoquastic-preserving, perturbative gadgets can be constructed, without an increase to particle dimension.

.
tldr: This paper proves that the 2-Local Stoquastic Hamiltonian problem on a 2D square lattice is StoqMA-complete, using spatially sparse circuits and perturbative gadgets.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of local Hamiltonian problems is fundamental to quantum computing, and stoquastic Hamiltonians are particularly relevant for quantum Monte Carlo methods.
method: The authors extend Oliveira and Terhal's spatially sparse circuit construction and Bravyi et al.'s perturbative gadgets to show StoqMA-completeness while preserving stoquasticity and geometry.
result: They demonstrate that StoqMA circuits can be made spatially sparse and that geometrical, stoquastic-preserving perturbative gadgets exist without increasing particle dimension.
conclusion: The 2D 2-local stoquastic Hamiltonian problem is StoqMA-complete, establishing a complexity classification for this physically relevant class.

title: Geometry-resolved Suppression Of Patch-potential Heating In Skeleton-electrode Ion Traps
authors: Chon-Teng Belmiro Chu, Hao-Chung Chen, Ting Hsu, Hsiang-Yu Lo, Ming-Shien Chang And Guin-Dar Lin
abstract: We present a quantitative, geometry-resolved framework to evaluate the effects of patch-potential noise in realistic three-dimensional Paul-trap structures. As a concrete application, we analyze a skeleton-electrode architecture and compare its performance against a conventional blade trap under identical ion-to-electrode distances and matched confinement parameters. The skeleton geometry achieves a suppression of motional heating exceeding 50%, with heating rate ratios of for the axial mode and for the radial mode. Patch-by-patch heating maps reveal that over 99% of the noise contribution originates from electrode surfaces within 500 m of the ion. We identify that axial heating follows a non-monotonic profile, with dominant ‘hotspots’ located at an intermediate distance of approximately 110 m. This behavior is driven by the vectorial directionality of the electric-field components, which provide the strongest axial coupling at these intermediate regions. Guided by these maps, we demonstrate a proof-of-principle electrode reconfiguration where segmented gaps are aligned with identified hotspots. This strategy successfully reduces axial heating even when the total electrode surface area increases, confirming that the spatial distribution of noise coupling—rather than total conductor area—is the primary driver of motional heating. These findings establish geometry-guided design as a practical route to suppress heating in trapped-ion platform, and the proposed skeleton architecture is compatible with advanced fabrication techniques, including metal additive manufacturing.
tldr: A geometry-resolved framework to suppress patch-potential heating in ion traps by optimizing electrode design, demonstrated with a skeleton-electrode architecture.
motivation: Motional heating from patch potentials limits trapped-ion quantum computing performance; understanding and mitigating this noise is crucial for improving qubit coherence.
method: Quantitative modeling of patch-potential noise in 3D Paul traps, comparing skeleton-electrode and blade trap geometries, with patch-by-patch heating maps and electrode reconfiguration.
result: Skeleton geometry suppresses heating by over 50%; axial heating hotspots identified at ~110 μm; reconfiguring gaps to align with hotspots reduces heating even with increased electrode area.
conclusion: Spatial distribution of noise coupling, not total conductor area, dominates heating; geometry-guided design offers a practical route to suppress heating in trapped-ion platforms.

title: A Quantum Kinetic Theory Of Photon Bose–Einstein Condensation In Semiconductors
authors: José L Figueiredo, Ross C Schofield, Ming Fu, Robert A Nyman, Rupert Oulton, Hugo Terças And Florian Mintert
abstract: Photon condensation in semiconductor microcavities is a transformative technique for engineering quantum states of light at room temperature by tailoring strong but incoherent light-matter interactions. While continuous-wave and electrical pumping offer exceptional prospects for miniaturized quantum photonic technologies, harnessing these requires conceptual advances in understanding non-equilibrium light-matter dynamics in semiconductors. We resolve this challenge through an ab initio quantum kinetic theory capturing how Coulomb interactions of optically excited carriers and phonon scattering mediate photon thermalization and condensation in semiconductors. Our microscopic model shows that at high carrier densities, thermalization is dominated by carrier–carrier Coulomb scattering, in clear contrast to the rovibrational relaxation that governs dye-based photon condensates. The theory predicts a rich nonequilibrium phase diagram with thermal, Bose-condensed, multimode, and lasing phases, quantitatively in agreement with recent experiments. Crucially, we identify how cavity detuning controls transitions between equilibrium and gain-dominated regimes, enabling tailored design of coherent light sources. This work thus provides the foundation for semiconductor-based quantum photonic devices operating beyond conventional laser paradigms.
tldr: A quantum kinetic theory of photon Bose-Einstein condensation in semiconductors, focusing on non-equilibrium light-matter dynamics.
motivation: To understand and control photon condensation in semiconductor microcavities for quantum photonic technologies.
method: Ab initio quantum kinetic theory incorporating Coulomb interactions and phonon scattering.
result: Identifies carrier-carrier Coulomb scattering as dominant thermalization mechanism at high densities, predicts phase diagram with thermal, condensed, multimode, and lasing phases.
conclusion: Provides foundation for semiconductor-based quantum photonic devices beyond conventional lasers.

title: Fate Of The Ising Universality Class Under Nonreciprocal Interactions
authors: M. Akritidis, A. Garc\'es, A. Vasilopoulos, M. Carosi, D. Levis, N. G. Fytas
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06981v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the critical behavior of a two-dimensional Ising model with nonreciprocal vision-cone interactions, which explicitly violate reciprocity and detailed balance. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations and dynamic renormalization-group analysis show that the asymptotic critical exponents remain fully consistent with the equilibrium Ising universality class over a broad range of nonreciprocal coupling strengths [MATH]. In contrast, dimensionless quantities such as the Binder cumulant and the correlation-length ratio display pronounced anisotropic nonequilibrium corrections and systematically deviate from their equilibrium Ising values. The renormalization-group flow further demonstrates that the nonreciprocal perturbation is irrelevant at the Wilson-Fisher fixed point while generating a finite shift of the critical temperature proportional to [MATH]. Our results demonstrate the remarkable robustness of two-dimensional Ising criticality against this class of directional interactions.
tldr: The 2D Ising model with nonreciprocal interactions remains in the equilibrium Ising universality class, but shows anisotropic nonequilibrium corrections.
motivation: To understand how nonreciprocal interactions, which break detailed balance, affect critical behavior in a paradigmatic statistical mechanics model.
method: Extensive Monte Carlo simulations and dynamic renormalization-group analysis.
result: Asymptotic critical exponents are consistent with equilibrium Ising, but dimensionless quantities like Binder cumulant deviate; the nonreciprocal perturbation is irrelevant at the Wilson-Fisher fixed point.
conclusion: Two-dimensional Ising criticality is robust against this class of directional interactions, with only finite shifts in critical temperature.

title: Information Theoretic Measures Of Isotropic Dunkl Oscillator In Spherical Coordinates
authors: Akash Halder, Amlan K. Roy, Debraj Nath
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An information theoretic analysis is done for the isotropic harmonic oscillator potential within the Dunkl-Schr\"odinger framework in spherical coordinates. Starting from the exact analytical eigensolution, various quantum information measures such as Shannon entropy, R\'enyi information, Tsallis entropy are derived. Besides, their relative measures like relative Shannon, relative R\'enyi, relative Tsallis as well as corresponding divergences (Jensen-Shannon, Jensen-R\'enyi, Jensen-Tsallis) are also obtained. In order to get Shannon entropy, a novel factorization method is introduced. This is facilitated through the use of well-known weighted Lebesgue measure. The results from the Dunkl case agree exactly with the non-Dunkl scenario, when Dunkl parameters vanish. The reflection operators and Dunkl parameters considerably influence the above measures. These are portrayed in graphical forms.
tldr: This paper computes information-theoretic measures (Shannon, Rényi, Tsallis entropies) for the isotropic Dunkl oscillator in spherical coordinates.
motivation: To extend quantum information measures to systems with reflection operators (Dunkl formalism) and study the effect of Dunkl parameters on these measures.
method: Exact analytical eigensolutions are obtained for the Dunkl-Schrödinger equation in spherical coordinates; a novel factorization method using weighted Lebesgue measure is introduced to compute Shannon entropy.
result: Analytical expressions for Shannon, Rényi, Tsallis entropies and their relative measures are derived; results reduce to the standard harmonic oscillator when Dunkl parameters vanish.
conclusion: The Dunkl parameters and reflection operators significantly influence the information measures, but the work is primarily a mathematical extension without direct connection to core quantum information topics like entanglement or cryptography.

title: Construction And Decoding Of Quantum Margulis Codes
authors: Michele Pacenti, Dimitris Chytas, And Bane Vasić
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2101 (2026).

Quantum low-density parity-check codes are a promising approach to fault-tolerant quantum computation, offering potential advantages in rate and decoding efficiency. In this work, we introduce quantum Margulis codes, a new class of QLDPC codes derived from Margulis' classical LDPC construction via the two-block group algebra framework. We show that quantum Margulis codes, unlike bivariate bicycle codes which require ordered statistics decoding for effective error correction, can be efficiently decoded using a standard min-sum decoder with linear complexity, when decoded under the code capacity noise model. This is attributed to their Tanner graph structure, which does not exhibit group symmetry, thereby mitigating the well-known problem of error degeneracy in QLDPC decoding. To further enhance performance, we propose an algorithm for constructing 2BGA codes with controlled girth, ensuring a minimum girth of 6 or 8, and use it to generate several quantum Margulis codes of length 240 and 642. We validate our approach through numerical simulations, demonstrating that quantum Margulis codes behave significantly better than BB codes in the error floor region, under min-sum decoding.

.
tldr: Introduces quantum Margulis codes, a new class of QLDPC codes with efficient min-sum decoding and improved error floor performance.
motivation: To construct QLDPC codes that can be decoded with linear complexity while avoiding error degeneracy, which plagues bivariate bicycle codes.
method: Derives codes from Margulis' classical LDPC construction using the two-block group algebra framework and proposes an algorithm to control girth.
result: Quantum Margulis codes of length 240 and 642 achieve better error floor performance than BB codes under min-sum decoding.
conclusion: These codes offer a practical alternative for fault-tolerant quantum computation with efficient decoding.

title: Quantum Cellular Automata On Symmetric Subalgebras
authors: Ruochen Ma, Yabo Li, And Meng Cheng
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2123 (2026).

We investigate quantum cellular automata (QCA) on one-dimensional spin systems defined over a subalgebra of the full local operator algebra – the symmetric subalgebra under a finite Abelian group symmetry [MATH]. For systems where each site carries a regular representation of [MATH], we establish a complete classification of such subalgebra QCAs based on two topological invariants: (1) a surjective homomorphism from the group of subalgebra QCAs to the group of anyon permutation symmetries in a [MATH] [MATH] gauge theory; and (2) a generalization of the Gross-Nesme-Vogts-Werner (GNVW) index that characterizes the flow of the symmetric subalgebra. Specifically, two subalgebra QCAs correspond to the same anyon permutation and share the same index if and only if they differ by a finite-depth unitary circuit composed of [MATH]-symmetric local gates. We also identify a set of operations that generate all subalgebra QCAs through finite compositions. As an example, we examine the Kramers-Wannier duality on a [MATH] symmetric subalgebra, demonstrating that it maps to the [MATH]-[MATH] permutation in the two-dimensional toric code and has an irrational index of [MATH]. Therefore, it cannot be extended to a QCA over the full local operator algebra and mixes nontrivially with lattice translations.

.
tldr: Classifies quantum cellular automata on symmetric subalgebras using topological invariants and shows the Kramers-Wannier duality has irrational index.
motivation: To understand the structure and classification of quantum cellular automata that respect a symmetry, which is a topic in quantum information theory but not a core focus.
method: Uses algebraic methods to define invariants (anyon permutation and generalized GNVW index) for subalgebra QCAs and relates them to finite-depth symmetric circuits.
result: Establishes a complete classification of subalgebra QCAs for finite Abelian group symmetries, and demonstrates that the Kramers-Wannier duality cannot be extended to a full QCA.
conclusion: The work provides a classification framework for symmetric QCAs, but is more mathematical and less directly applicable to the user's core interests in entanglement, nonlocality, or cryptography.

title: Cyclic Ladder Operators And Hidden Weyl-Heisenberg Structure In A Floquet System
authors: Li Ge Tianao Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ladder operators, found in the quantum harmonic oscillator and other quantized systems, provide an elegant approach to solving or understanding otherwise intricate physics problems. In this Letter, we discuss cyclic ladder operators in both Hermitian and non-Hermitian systems with a finite Hilbert space, with the highest (lowest) level directly descending (ascending) to the lowest (highest) level via a single raising (lowering) operation. We show that an equally spaced energy ladder emerges when these systems have an underlying Weyl-Heisenberg commutation relation, with the cyclic ladder operators and the temporal evolution operator behaving as the generators of the Weyl-Heisenberg group. We further illustrate such a system using a one-dimensional Floquet lattice, where the cyclic ladder operators become diagonal and the temporal evolution simplifies to a permutation matrix after a Floquet period. Our findings reveal a hidden relation between non-trivial dynamics and algebraic principles in Floquet systems, which may exist for other quantum numbers as well besides the energy levels.
tldr: This paper introduces cyclic ladder operators in finite Hilbert spaces and reveals a hidden Weyl-Heisenberg structure in a Floquet system.
motivation: To generalize ladder operators to cyclic systems and uncover algebraic structures underlying Floquet dynamics.
method: The authors define cyclic ladder operators for Hermitian and non-Hermitian systems with finite Hilbert space, show that equally spaced energy ladders arise from a Weyl-Heisenberg commutation relation, and illustrate with a one-dimensional Floquet lattice.
result: Cyclic ladder operators and the temporal evolution operator generate the Weyl-Heisenberg group; in the Floquet lattice, the evolution becomes a permutation matrix after one period.
conclusion: The work reveals a hidden algebraic structure in Floquet systems that may apply to other quantum numbers beyond energy.
